Saving example.com:8080 succeeds, but a request from http://example.com:8080 produces URI.host equal to example.com and never matches that record, disabling embedding and retrieval for the configured host. Use a consistent port representation in both storage and lookup.

The validator accepts hosts such as `example.com:8080`, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host (`example.com`) and compares it to the stored port-qualified string. An accepted and saved host therefore never authorizes its corresponding URLs. Normalize the stored and queried authority consistently, including a deliberate port policy.

issues.descricao: Claims expandable_first_post? lost its 'embeddable hosts configured' guard and now expands first posts when no EmbeddableHost exists.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `expandable_first_post?` dropped the `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?` guard and now returns true whenever `embed_truncate?` and `has_topic_embed?` are true, with no check that any embeddable host is actually configured. WHY: a topic whose embed was created by a host that has since been deleted still gets its first post expanded, changing embed output for a state the previous guard blocked; the retained "is false if embeddable_host is blank" spec no longer exercises host presence (has_topic_embed? is unstubbed/false), so this regression is not caught. HOW: gate on the new source of truth, e.g. `EmbeddableHost.exists? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` if host presence is still required.

expandable_first_post? used to return false when no embeddable hosts were configured. The new version drops that guard (`SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present?`) and does not replace it with `EmbeddableHost.exists?`. A forum with no embeddable hosts but with embed_truncate on and a topic embed now gets an expandable first post. Restore the guard by checking `EmbeddableHost.exists?`.

WHAT: expandable_first_post? dropped the hosts-present guard and now returns true for any embedded topic even with zero EmbeddableHost rows. WHY: UI offers expand on first post when embedding is effectively unconfigured, a regression from SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? check.

issues.descricao: Claims the plural *_ids hydration branch crashes on non-array values and keeps undefined entries for missing ids.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: plural branch calls obj[k].map without checking it is an array and keeps undefined entries for missing ids. WHY: null/non-array *_ids payload or dangling id crashes hydration or yields array with undefined models instead of filtering/fallback.

issues.descricao: Claims Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing, so the client's saveChanges appears to succeed without saving.

comentarios.texto: The update action does not change or persist anything and only re-renders the embedding. The client's saveChanges therefore appears to succeed while doing nothing.

issues.descricao: Claims EmbeddingSerializer emits only embeddable_host_ids without sideloading the host records, so the admin host table renders empty.

comentarios.texto: `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids` emits only `embeddable_host_ids` in the show/update response and never sideloads the EmbeddableHost records. The admin client, however, consumes `embedding.embeddable_hosts` as full objects (store.js `_hydrateEmbedded` looks each id up via `_lookupSubType` and assigns the resolved records; `embedding.hbs` iterates them and `embeddable-host.hbs` reads `host.host`/`host.category`). With ids-only and no concurrent sideload, `_lookupSubType` resolves nothing, so the host table renders empty on first load of /admin/customize/embedding. Embed the objects (e.g. `embed: :ids, include: true`, or `embed: :objects`) so the payload carries the `embeddable_hosts` records the client now requires.

`has_many :embeddable_hosts, ..., embed: :ids` without `include: true` emits only `embeddable_host_ids` and never sideloads the embedded objects, but the consumer `store._hydrateEmbedded` resolves those ids through `_lookupSubType`, which reads `root['embeddable_hosts']`. With the collection absent every id hydrates to `undefined`, so the admin embedding page shows no/blank hosts. Add `include: true` so the collection the store requires is actually serialized.

sugestoes.texto: Making .contents a flex container leaves the header-extra-info component's outer Ember div with the default min-width:auto. The topic title inside it uses white-space:nowrap, and overflow:hidden is only on the nested .extra-info-wrapper, so a long title prevents the actual flex item from shrinking and pushes the navigation panel beyond the header instead of truncating the title. Set min-width:0 on the direct header-extra-info flex item (for example by assigning a class to that component wrapper), so the existing inner overflow and ellipsis rules can constrain the title.

issues.descricao: The flex-item styles target the inner .extra-info-wrapper instead of the component's root div, so in the flexbox header a long topic title keeps its full width and pushes the navigation panel out instead of being truncated.

comentarios.texto: The flex-item styling targets the inner .extra-info-wrapper rather than the outer div generated by header-extra-info's Ember.Component. With .contents now using flexbox, that outer div retains its automatic minimum width, so a long nowrap topic title cannot shrink to the available space and pushes the navigation panel outside the header instead of being ellipsized by the existing desktop truncation rules. Move the extra-info-wrapper class onto the component's root element and set min-width: 0 on that flex item so ordering and truncation apply to the actual header child.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits no -moz-box-align, so on old Firefox versions using the display:-moz-box fallback the advertised vertical centering is not applied.

comentarios.texto: The alignment mixin does not match the Mozilla fallback emitted by flexbox(): when display: -moz-box is selected, neither align-items nor the WebKit/MS declarations control its cross-axis alignment. Consequently @include align-items(center) in the header and small-action leaves those children at the legacy default instead of vertically centering them. Emit -moz-box-align: $alignment alongside -webkit-box-align so the advertised fallback produces the same alignment.

issues.descricao: The align-items mixin emits -ms-align-items, which never existed in IE/Edge; the legacy property is -ms-flex-align, so the declaration is dead.
issues.textoGolden: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: align-items() mixin emits -ms-align-items: $alignment which is not a valid IE10/11 property (only -ms-flex-align exists). WHY: dead declaration shows wrong contract and leaves IE alignment dependent solely on -ms-flex-align, which also breaks for flex-start/flex-end values. HOW: remove the -ms-align-items line and map flex-start/flex-end to start/end for -ms-flex-align/-webkit-box-align.

issues.descricao: Removing the float-based right alignment of .d-header .panel leaves the server-rendered (no-JS) header's login panel, which sits inside .row and is not a flex item, no longer right-aligned next to the title.
issues.textoGolden: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

issues.descricao: Claims the order mixin's box-ordinal-group values are off by one versus order, so legacy WebKit/Firefox render a different item order.
issues.textoGolden: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `@mixin order($val)` emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val`, but the old `-webkit-box` flexbox model's `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based (default 1) while modern `order` is 0-based (default 0). WHY: the value is off by one on old WebKit engines, so the mixin does not reproduce the ordering the caller intends — the mixin exists precisely to give consistent ordering across prefixes, and callers `@include order(2)` (topic.scss:30) and `@include order(3)` (header.scss:39) will get the equivalent of `order: 1` and `order: 2` respectively on those engines, making their relative position against modern browsers inconsistent. HOW: emit `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1;` (and keep `-ms-flex-order`/`-webkit-order`/`order` as-is, since those are 0-based).

The `order($val)` mixin passes the same `$val` to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` and to `order`/`-webkit-order`/`-ms-flex-order`, but these properties use different bases: `order` (and its flexbox prefixes) is 0-based with default 0, whereas the legacy `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` (old `display: -webkit-box` model) is 1-based with default 1. So a call like `@include order(3)` (header.scss:39) emits `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3` while `order: 3` — the element lands at a different relative position in the legacy engine than the mixin name/value implies, i.e. the declared order does not match the order actually applied. Emit `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: $val + 1` (and keep `-moz-box-ordinal-group` consistent) so both properties produce the same position.

The `order()` mixin passes `$val` unchanged to `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but those legacy box properties are 1-based with a default of 1, while standard `order` is 0-based with a default of 0. The value is therefore off by one in the legacy engines: e.g. `order(0)` (or `order(1)`) would place the element before all default-order siblings in old WebKit/Gecko instead of leaving it where it is. Emit `$val + 1` for the two box-ordinal-group declarations (and keep `$val` for `-ms-flex-order`/`order`) so the prefixed fallbacks preserve the same ordering as the standard property.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The second definition of downsize replaces the existing five-argument method instead of adding an overload. WHY: Jobs::ResizeEmoji.execute still calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts), which now raises ArgumentError and prevents emoji resizing. HOW: Use a single method that supports both the geometry-string and width/height calling conventions, or give the geometry-string helper a distinct name.

WHAT: The fixed 10 MB client limit applies to attachments as well as images. WHY: On sites with max_attachment_size_kb above 10240, previously valid attachments are now rejected in the browser even though UploadValidator permits them and the feature only requires a new image input limit. HOW: Apply the fixed limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

WHAT: The downsizing loop ignores a false result from OptimizedImage.downsize and retries the unchanged input. WHY: convert_with returns false for conversion failures, so a malformed or unsupported oversized image triggers five identical external conversion attempts before proceeding to upload validation. HOW: Break out of the loop when downsize returns false.

Ruby does not overload methods by argument count: this definition replaces the width/height version immediately above. The existing ResizeEmoji job calls OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts), so it now raises ArgumentError instead of resizing emoji. Preserve both calling forms with a single dispatching method or use a different name for the geometry-string helper.

Ruby does not overload methods by arity: this definition replaces the width/height version immediately above it. The existing consumer in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`, which now raises ArgumentError (five arguments supplied, three or four expected), breaking emoji resizing. Preserve both calling conventions with one dispatching method or give the dimensions-based helper a distinct name.

issues.descricao: downsize is defined twice in OptimizedImage; the new (from, to, dimensions, opts) version overrides the (max_width, max_height) one, so existing callers such as ResizeEmoji that pass width and height now raise ArgumentError.
issues.textoGolden: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: A second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined that overrides the existing `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` at lines 145-147. WHY: Ruby uses the last definition, so the effective downsize now only accepts 3-4 args, and the existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 (`OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)`) passes 5 args and raises ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, given 5, expected 3..4), breaking emoji resizing. HOW: Remove the duplicate; keep a single downsize method whose signature matches all callers (the 4-arg uploads_controller call `downsize(path, path, "80%", allow_animation: ...)` and the 5-arg ResizeEmoji call), or rename one of them.

`downsize` is defined twice: the original 5-param form `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at lines 145-147 and the new 4-param form `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` at lines 149-151. Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the effective signature is now 4 params and the 5-param version is dead code. The pre-existing consumer app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 positional args, which now raises ArgumentError on every emoji resize. Either update that caller to the new `dimensions` form or remove the redundant override so the old signature keeps working.

`self.downsize` is defined twice in the same class scope (line 145 `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and the new line 149 `(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`). Ruby keeps only the last definition, so the 4-argument version is dead and unreachable. The existing caller `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` in app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 passes 5 arguments and will now raise ArgumentError (expected 3..4). Remove the duplicate definition (keep only the `dimensions`-based one, or convert resize_emoji's call), otherwise emoji resizing breaks.

issues.descricao: The client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB instead of the per-type max_<type>_size_kb setting, so attachment limits diverge from the server: larger allowed attachments are blocked and smaller limits are only enforced server-side.
issues.textoGolden: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

comentarios.texto: Hardcoded max size literal 10 * 1024 replaces site-setting-derived max size. Behavioral concern outside assigned class.

The fixed 10 MB client limit is applied to attachments as well as images, replacing max_attachment_size_kb. Sites configured to allow attachments larger than 10 MB can no longer upload those valid files through the composer, although UploadValidator still permits them. Apply the new input ceiling only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.

WHAT: Client check hardcodes maxSizeKB to 10*1024 instead of Discourse.SiteSettings['max_'+type+'_size_kb'], losing image vs attachment distinction. WHY: Sites with smaller max_attachment_size_kb pass client validation then fail server-side, and sites with limits >10MB incorrectly block valid uploads with wrong max_size_kb message. HOW: Restore per-type SiteSetting lookup (keep 10MB only as image downsize ceiling).

issues.descricao: The upload downsizing passes a percentage ('80%') as dimensions, but for animated GIFs the gifsicle path uses --resize-fit, which expects WxH geometry, so downsizing silently fails.
issues.textoGolden: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.

comentarios.texto: The controller passes the percentage string `"80%"` as the dimensions argument to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, but the consumer requires explicit `WxH` geometry: the code this PR deleted built exactly `"#{width}x#{height}"`, and the animated path runs `gifsicle --resize-fit #{dimensions}`, which rejects a percentage. Pass an explicit size (e.g. a computed `"WxH"` from the max KB target) so the auto-downsize actually reduces the file, rather than silently no-oping and leaving oversized uploads.

Caller passes "80%" as dimensions to OptimizedImage.downsize, but the downsize/optimize instruction builders in optimized_image.rb expect explicit "WxH" geometry (interpolated as -resize #{dimensions}\>). A bare percentage does not satisfy that contract and will produce a malformed geometry. Fix the caller to supply WxH dimensions or add explicit percentage handling to the callee.

issues.descricao: Auto-downsizing passes the upload tempfile path, which lacks a .gif extension, so the animated branch is never chosen and convert keeps only the first frame, flattening oversized animated GIFs.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new auto-downsize call passes a tempfile path whose name has no `.GIF` extension, so `optimize` never selects the animated branch (`method_name += "_animated" if opts[:allow_animation] && from =~ /\.GIF$/i`) and uses `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert from[0]` and keeps only the first frame. WHY: Animated GIFs larger than max_image_size_kb that are uploaded through this path have their animation flattened to a single frame even though SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. HOW: Detect the image type from the original filename/content-type rather than the tempfile path (or pass a flag) so the gifsicle animated downsize path is used for GIF inputs.

Passing the multipart tempfile path to downsize prevents animation detection when that path does not end in .gif, even when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled. OptimizedImage.optimize checks the path suffix and otherwise uses convert with input[0], so oversized animated GIF uploads are permanently flattened to their first frame. Preserve the original image extension in the processing path or pass the image format explicitly to select animated processing.

issues.descricao: The comment promises images are reduced to the allowed size, but the loop only tries five 80% reductions with no guarantee of reaching the limit.

comentarios.texto: The comment says large images are "automatically reduced to allowed size", but the loop only resizes by 80% up to 5 attempts (≈0.33× of the original in the best case) and then stops without any check that the result actually meets `max_image_size_kb`. The prose promises a guarantee the code does not provide; either make the loop actually converge to the allowed size or reword the comment to state that the image is only attempted to be reduced.

issues.descricao: The downsize retry loop ignores the false return of a failed conversion and repeats the same failing ImageMagick call up to five times.

comentarios.texto: The retry loop ignores downsize's false return value and retries failed conversions while the file remains oversized. convert_with returns false on converter failure, so an unsupported or malformed oversized image launches the same failing external conversion up to five times per upload without any changed input. Break on a failed downsize result and return an upload error rather than repeating the conversion.

WHAT: Downsize loop ignores OptimizedImage.downsize return value and retries up to 5 times unconditionally while checking tempfile.size. WHY: Failed converts (e.g. SVG, invalid 80%> geometry, corrupt image) burn 5 ImageMagick runs then Upload.create_for still runs with oversized/unmodified file and fails validation, wasting CPU and breaking the feature. HOW: Break on false return and handle failure.

issues.descricao: Claims up to five synchronous ImageMagick runs per oversized upload block request threads and enable DoS.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Up to 5 synchronous OptimizedImage.downsize + ImageOptim convert runs execute inline in create_upload request cycle for every oversized image. WHY: Blocks the Rails request thread with CPU-intensive shell-outs per upload, enabling easy request-thread exhaustion/DoS with large images. HOW: Move downsizing to background job or enforce single-pass/timeout.

issues.descricao: Claims the downsize loop checking tempfile.size may never terminate because of a stale cached size, causing infinite loops.
issues.textoGolden: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

issues.descricao: Claims the API URL download limit changed from max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10 MB, amplifying SSRF bandwidth.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: API URL download limit changed from SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb to hardcoded 10.megabytes. WHY: Allows an API caller to force the server to fetch up to 10MB from an arbitrary URL even when admin configured a much smaller cap, amplifying SSRF bandwidth/disk usage. HOW: Keep download cap tied to min/max of settings or enforce admin cap.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: totalPages adds an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit. WHY: with 50 members and a limit of 50, the UI displays two pages and enables Next, which requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. HOW: calculate the page count with Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

WHAT: the public members route now loads a single 50-member page without providing a way to retrieve subsequent pages. WHY: findMembers sends the model's default limit of 50, and discourse/templates/group/members.hbs only renders members without navigation or load-more actions, so members beyond the first 50 become inaccessible for custom groups that previously returned the complete list. HOW: add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and call findMembers, as the admin page now does.

When user_count is an exact positive multiple of limit, floor(count / limit) + 1 overcounts pages. For example, 50 members with limit 50 reports two pages, leaves Next enabled on the first page, and allows fetching offset 50, which contains no members. Use the ceiling of the ratio to count pages.

For any positive member count that is an exact multiple of the limit, this reports an extra page. For example, 50 members with limit 50 displays 1/2 and leaves Next enabled; clicking it requests offset 50 and displays an empty member list. Use ceiling division so showingLast agrees with the actual number of pages.

This now paginates every group to 50 members, whereas custom groups previously returned their entire membership. The public group-members route calls findMembers() once, and group/members.hbs only renders members without pagination controls or further requests. Consequently, users can no longer see members beyond the first 50 of a custom group (and automatic groups also drop from the previous default 200 to 50). Update the public consumer to navigate or fetch subsequent pages when introducing this endpoint contract.

Every completed request overwrites members, offset, and user_count without checking whether it is still current. For example, start a pagination request, then remove a member while that request is in flight. The removal triggers a second findMembers request; if that newer response arrives first and the original response arrives last, the deleted member and old count are restored in the displayed model. Rapid next/previous navigation can likewise revert the selected page. Assign each fetch a generation token and apply results only if it is still the latest request.

The public members view now renders the model's paginated `members` array, but the matching change to `Group#findMembers` requests only 50 users and replaces that array with a single page. The next/previous actions and controls introduced by this PR are only on the admin screen. Consequently, public group pages with more than 50 members silently show only the first 50, with no way to reach the remaining users (previously nonautomatic groups returned all members). Wire pagination into this public view/controller as well, or preserve full-list loading for this consumer.

issues.descricao: The admin group pager computes total pages as floor(user_count / limit) + 1, so when the member count is an exact multiple of the limit it shows an extra page and Next navigates to an empty member list.
issues.textoGolden: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.

comentarios.texto: totalPages (and currentPage) use `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which is an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members, limit 50 → reports 2 pages although only 1 exists). This leaves `showingLast` false on the real last page, so 'next' navigates to an empty page at offset=user_count. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and compute currentPage consistently) to get the correct page count.

totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit: `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` gives 2 for user_count=50, limit=50, although 50 members occupy exactly one page. Correct it to `Math.ceil(this.get('user_count') / this.get('limit'))`. Effect: for a group whose member count is a multiple of the page size, totalPages is one too high, showingLast remains false so the 'next' link stays enabled, and clicking it navigates to a phantom empty page.

`totalPages` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts by one whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50 members with limit 50 yields 2 pages instead of 1). Since `showingLast` is `propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`, on a full last page `showingLast` is false, so the `next` action stays enabled and advances `offset` to `user_count`, rendering an empty page labeled as the last page. Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero-member guard) so the count matches the real number of pages.

issues.descricao: Several Group model functions (findMembers, destroy, userCountDisplay) return a value on some paths and undefined on others, triggering consistent-return lint warnings.
issues.textoGolden: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

issues.descricao: Paging actions fire overlapping member requests and each response unconditionally overwrites offset and members, so a stale response arriving last can revert the list to an earlier page.

comentarios.texto: Guard against stale member-fetch responses before updating the model. `next` updates offset immediately and leaves navigation enabled, so with at least three pages two rapid clicks issue requests for offsets 50 and 100. If the offset-100 response arrives first and the offset-50 response arrives last, this unconditional `setProperties` resets both offset and members to the older page, undoing the latest navigation. Refreshes after membership changes can similarly be overwritten by an earlier fetch. Track a per-model request generation and apply only the latest response, or serialize navigation and refresh requests.

issues.descricao: The public members endpoint now always caps results at 50 per page, but the public group members page has no pagination, so groups with more than 50 members are silently truncated for users.

comentarios.texto: The public members route now loads only the model's default 50-member page without providing any way to request subsequent pages. The public group/members.hbs template only renders members and has no Next/Previous controls, so members after the first 50 become inaccessible (manual groups previously returned all members). Add public pagination controls and actions that update offset and reload members.

The new default limit applies to nonautomatic groups as well, but the public group-members route still calls findMembers() only once and its template simply iterates members without pagination. Previously this endpoint returned every member of a nonautomatic group; now a group with more than 50 members exposes only the first 50 on its public members page, with no way to reach the rest. Update that consumer to fetch subsequent pages or provide pagination when introducing this endpoint contract.

Provide pagination or load subsequent pages for the public group-members view. findMembers now requests only 50 members, and this route calls it only once while its template simply iterates members without navigation. Custom groups previously returned all members, so groups larger than 50 now have members that cannot be viewed on this page.

issues.descricao: Creating a group ignores the alias_level the admin selected, saving only name and visibility, so new groups keep the default alias level.

comentarios.texto: Persist params[:alias_level] when creating a group, just as update does. The creation form exposes aliasLevelOptions and group.asJSON sends the selected alias_level, but create saves only name and visible. A newly created group therefore retains the default alias level instead of the administrator's selection.

issues.descricao: Removing a member deletes the membership row directly and skips clearing the user's primary_group_id, so a removed user can keep this group as their primary group.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the Group#remove destroy path. WHY: bypasses GroupUser destroy callbacks and primary_group_id cleanup done in destroy_deletions, leaving stale membership side-effects (e.g. dangling primary_group_id). HOW: load the User and call group.remove(user).

Removing a member with group.users.delete bypasses the primary_group_id cleanup previously performed by Group#destroy_deletions during usernames updates. A user whose primary group is this group remains associated with it as their primary group after membership removal, leaving stale primary-group state used by user administration and post serialization. Clear primary_group_id for the removed user when it equals this group's id as part of the removal operation.

issues.descricao: The remove_member spec issues a PUT request although the route only maps DELETE to remove_member, so the test uses a verb never routed in production.
issues.textoGolden: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

comentarios.texto: This example sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the PR maps `remove_member` only to DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`); PUT on that path routes to `groups#add_members`. Controller specs bypass the router, so the example still lands on `remove_member` and passes regardless — it would still pass if the DELETE route were missing or wired to the wrong action, leaving the newly introduced verb/action pairing untested. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member`, as the sibling example at line 125 already does.

The test 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' sends `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but the route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. It exercises the action with a verb that is never routed in production. Use `xhr :delete, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42` so the test matches the real request.

issues.descricao: Claims the now-unawaited findMembers() call creates a race where the controller has no member data available when it needs it.
issues.textoGolden: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

issues.descricao: Claims the public group members template iterates a bare members property that resolves to undefined because the controller's model is now the Group object.

comentarios.texto: setupController now sets controller model to the Group object (not the members array), but template iterates bare `members`. Expose the new shape to the template (e.g. controller.set('members', model.get('members')) with observer/alias, or iterate `model.members`) — otherwise `{{#each m in members}}` resolves to undefined and the members list never renders.

issues.descricao: Claims add_members/remove_member read params[:group_id] while the route supplies the group id as params[:id], so the actions always fail with ParameterMissing.
issues.textoGolden: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

comentarios.texto: add_members reads params.require(:group_id) but the member route declared in config/routes.rb supplies params[:id] (JS calls /admin/groups/:id/members.json). Request always raises ParameterMissing. Change to Group.find(params.require(:id).to_i) or accept either key.
remove_member reads params.require(:group_id) but the member route supplies params[:id]. Same ParameterMissing on every DELETE /admin/groups/:id/members request. Change to params.require(:id).

add_members and remove_member read the group id via `params.require(:group_id)`, but the routes that expose them (config/routes.rb:49-50, `delete/put "members"` inside `resources :groups`) are member routes that supply the parameter as `:id`. The front-end calls `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:42,53), so `params[:group_id]` is nil and `require` raises ActionController::ParameterMissing, returning 400 — add/remove member is broken in production. Use `params.require(:id)` (or read `params[:id]`) to match the route; the specs pass `group_id:` directly via xhr, which is why they don't catch this.

issues.descricao: Claims add_members does not strip whitespace around comma-separated usernames, so entries like 'alice, bob' silently fail to add members.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: add_members splits usernames on comma without stripping whitespace. WHY: input like "alice, bob" looks up " bob" (leading space) via find_by_username, silently fails, and still returns success_json so members are silently not added. HOW: strip each token and skip blanks before lookup.

issues.descricao: Claims the public members endpoint accepts an unbounded or negative limit/offset, letting a caller force loading and serializing the whole membership of a large group.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: members action takes attacker-controlled limit/offset with no max or negativity clamp. WHY: a request with limit=1000000 forces loading/serializing the entire membership table in one response, causing memory/CPU blowup on large groups. HOW: clamp limit to a max (e.g. min(limit, 200)) and floor offset/limit at 0.

The client-supplied limit is used with no upper bound, and a negative or zero value is not handled. A caller can request an arbitrarily large limit and force loading and serializing of every member of a large group in one request. Clamp it, for example limit = [[(params[:limit] || 50).to_i, 1].max, 200].min, and make offset non-negative.

sugestoes.texto: Fallback locales are preloaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths with unloaded fallback dictionaries. Jobs::Base sets the site locale and executes jobs without this filter, and post_alerter switches to a user's locale with I18n.with_locale; the accelerator loads only the active locale, while backend fallback lookups bypass that loader, so missing keys return missing translations instead of falling back to English or the site language in a fresh worker. Ensure the fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary rather than exclusively at the HTTP request boundary.

issues.descricao: Fallback locale catalogs are only loaded in the controller's set_locale filter, while translate loads just the current locale, so translations outside requests (jobs, mailers) cannot fall back to the site default or English.

comentarios.texto: Fallback catalogs are ensured loaded only in the controller filter, leaving non-controller translation paths without the catalogs required by the newly enabled fallback backend. Jobs::Base sets I18n.locale directly and PostAlerter uses I18n.with_locale, while the accelerator loads only the current locale and backend fallback lookups bypass that loader; missing keys therefore still produce missing translations or skip the configured site fallback until another request happens to load those catalogs. Ensure the full fallback chain is loaded at the translation boundary, rather than relying solely on the controller filter.

The new fallbacks contract requires the fallback locales (site default and :en, from FallbackLocaleList#[]) to be loaded before Backend::Simple#translate is asked for them — Backend::Simple only returns already-loaded translations. This PR added I18n.ensure_loaded!/I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! but wired it only into ApplicationController#set_locale, and the loader that actually gates every translation, I18n.translate (line 68), still loads only `config.locale`. As a result, any I18n.t performed outside the request cycle (console, background jobs, mailers) or before set_locale runs will not load the fallback locales and will silently return 'translation missing' instead of the fallback the new I18n.fallbacks advertises. Fix: have translate ensure the fallback chain is loaded (e.g. call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! / load the fallback locales here), not rely on the controller hook.

translate loads only config.locale, but the new fallback chain (default_locale, :en) is loaded only by the controller's I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!. Outside controllers (jobs, mailers, rake), a key missing in the current locale falls back to a locale that is not loaded, so it returns 'translation missing', and the LRU cache then stores that result. Fix: in translate, call I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded! (or load each locale in fallbacks[config.locale]) before the lookup.

issues.descricao: The translation cache key does not include the site or its default locale, but fallback results now depend on SiteSetting.default_locale, so multisite processes or a changed default locale serve stale fallback translations.

comentarios.texto: The new fallback order depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the accelerator's translation cache does not include that setting or the current site in its key. In a multisite process, two sites with the same user locale and different default locales reuse the first site's cached fallback translation; changing the default locale also leaves cached fallback results stale. Include the effective fallback chain or site/default-locale context in the translation cache key.

issues.descricao: Claims a fallback value cached for a not-yet-loaded locale stays stale after that locale's file is loaded, because ensure_loaded! does not invalidate the translation cache.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new ensure_loaded! loads fallback locale files but does not invalidate the accelerator's shared @cache (only reload! clears it on lines 39-43), while the initializer now enables I18n::Backend::Fallbacks so a lookup for a not-yet-loaded locale returns the :en/default value instead of raising MissingTranslation. WHY: That fallback value is cached by translate under the requested locale key (line 72-76); when ensure_loaded!/load_locale later loads the correct locale file (e.g. a background job at app/jobs/base.rb:151 sets I18n.locale and translates before the locale is loaded, then a web request loads it), the stale fallback string is still served from cache for that locale. HOW: clear @cache when newly loading a locale (e.g. set `@cache = nil` inside load_locale/ensure_loaded! after adding a locale to @loaded_locales, or include the loaded-locale state in the cache key).

issues.descricao: Suggests normalizing the locale because a String locale mixed with Symbol fallback entries defeats uniq and causes double lookups or double loading.
issues.textoGolden: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] mixes types — the incoming `locale` is left as-is (a String, since I18n.locale is set to User#effective_locale / SiteSetting.default_locale which are Strings) while the other two chain entries are Symbols (`SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym`, `:en`), so `.uniq` cannot deduplicate the current locale and returns e.g. ["en", :en]. WHY: I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate/#exists? iterate this array and call super for every entry, so the current locale is looked up a second time on each cache miss, and FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded! calls I18n.ensure_loaded! for both "en" and :en, making load_locale parse and merge the same .yml file twice on the first request. HOW: normalize the argument first, e.g. `locale = locale.to_sym` at the top of `[]` (or build `[locale.to_sym, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact`).

issues.descricao: Claims a nil default_locale makes FallbackLocaleList#[] raise NoMethodError on every missing translation.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] calls SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym before uniq.compact, so a nil/missing default_locale raises NoMethodError. WHY: crashes fallback resolution (every missing key) during boot, DB-down, or unset setting instead of falling back to :en. HOW: guard nil e.g. SiteSetting.default_locale.try(:to_sym) before building the chain.

issues.descricao: Claims every fallback lookup hits the database or Redis through SiteSetting.default_locale, amplifying per-request load.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: FallbackLocaleList#[] queries SiteSetting.default_locale on every fallbacks[locale] lookup. WHY: with fallbacks enabled every missing translation triggers a SiteSetting (DB/Redis) hit in the translate hot path, amplifying per-request query/load cost. HOW: memoize/cache the default-locale segment and invalidate only when the setting changes.

issues.descricao: Claims a user-controlled locale with regex metacharacters reaches load_locale's Regexp and forces loading of unintended locale files.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: New I18n.ensure_loaded!(locale) forwards the locale unchecked into load_locale which builds Regexp.new("\\.#{locale}\\.yml$") for load_path.grep. WHY: the locale chain includes user-controlled I18n.locale (current_user.effective_locale via FallbackLocaleList#ensure_loaded!), so regex metacharacters (e.g. .* ) widen the match and force loading of unintended/all locale files (resource exhaustion / unexpected translation loading). HOW: escape the locale with Regexp.escape and/or validate against LocaleSiteSetting.supported_locales before loading.

issues.descricao: Claims @loaded_locales is lazily initialized and shared across threads without synchronization.
issues.textoGolden: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

sugestoes.texto: Authenticate treats a cached tagging result as proof that a device is admitted, but tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. When the limit is full, the first request for a new device is denied while its cache entry remains; repeating the same request returns nil from the cache and grants anonymous access for the cache lifetime. Cache only successfully admitted devices, or remove the cache entry on every failed store operation before returning the error.

The new authentication limit is skipped entirely when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent because TagDevice returns nil immediately for an empty device ID. A client can omit this user-controlled header and receive an anonymous identity even when the configured device limit is full. When the limit is enabled, require a valid device identifier before granting anonymous access, using a compatible identification flow for initial browser requests.

The active-device count and the subsequent upsert are separate database operations with no admission lock or atomic capacity reservation. Concurrent requests with distinct new device IDs can both observe count below deviceLimit and insert successfully, exceeding the configured limit; the unique device_id index does not prevent this. Serialize capacity checking and admission with a database-backed lock or equivalent atomic mechanism that also works across Grafana instances.

tagDeviceUI sets localCache before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the new limit check rejects a device, this return propagates the error but leaves that cache entry intact. Retrying with the same device ID then hits the cache, returns nil, and Authenticate admits the device despite the full limit for the cache lifetime. Cache only successful store operations (or remove the entry on error).

CountDevices and the subsequent upsert are not an atomic admission operation. With one slot remaining, concurrent requests for distinct device IDs can both read count < deviceLimit and both insert successfully. This produces more active devices than the limit the new authentication path purports to enforce, including across Grafana instances. Serialize the count-and-insert admission decision using database-level coordination shared by instances.

The newly propagated limit error does not undo tagDeviceUI's cache write: that method calls localCache.SetDefault before CreateOrUpdateDevice, and returns nil immediately for cached devices. At capacity, the first request from a new device receives ErrDeviceLimitReached, but a retry with the same device key hits that cache entry and Authenticate accepts it for the cache lifetime without checking the limit. Cache only successful writes (and ensure concurrent callers cannot treat an in-flight write as success).

The count and subsequent upsert are separate operations with no serialization across them. With limit N and N-1 active devices, requests for two different new devices can both read N-1, both pass this check, and both insert, leaving N+1 admitted devices. This also applies across Grafana instances, so a process-local lock alone is insufficient. Serialize admission at the database level and perform the count and write within that protected operation.

issues.descricao: The device limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate non-atomic steps, so concurrent requests from new devices can all pass the check and exceed the configured limit.
issues.textoGolden: Race condition: Multiple concurrent requests could pass the device count check simultaneously and create devices beyond the limit. Consider using a database transaction or lock.

comentarios.texto: The limit check counts devices and then inserts in separate steps with no lock or transaction. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. Make the count-and-insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit.

The device limit check is a non-atomic count followed by an insert. Concurrent requests from different new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the number of devices exceeds deviceLimit. Make the check and insert atomic, for example with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*)) < limit, or serialize the check and insert under a lock.

WHAT: CreateOrUpdateDevice does check-then-act (CountDevices then INSERT/UPSERT) with no lock, transaction, or unique-guard when deviceLimit>0. WHY: Two concurrent new-device requests can both observe count < limit and both insert, exceeding the configured limit and breaking the enforcement contract. HOW: Enforce atomically (e.g., conditional insert guarded by count in one statement/transaction with serializable lock, or re-check count on conflict).

issues.descricao: Device slots are keyed by the client-controlled X-Grafana-Device-Id header with no validation or rate limiting, so an anonymous caller can fill the limit with fake IDs and deny anonymous access to every new legitimate device.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Device slots counted toward deviceLimit are keyed by the unauthenticated X-Grafana-Device-Id header (read in impl.go TagDevice) with no validation or rate-limit. WHY: Any anonymous caller can mint arbitrary device IDs to fill the table up to the limit, after which all legitimate new anonymous devices get ErrDeviceLimitReached and authentication is denied — a trivial anonymous-access DoS introduced by the limit. HOW: Do not let a single client consume many slots (e.g., bind slot consumption to IP/fingerprint, rate-limit new-device creation, or require proof of distinct device).

issues.descricao: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit and never verifies that an existing device can still be updated at the limit.

comentarios.texto: The at-limit call reuses a brand-new device ID ("keep") that was never inserted, so it only reaches updateDevice's `rowsAffected == 0` -> ErrDeviceLimitReached branch. The success branch of the newly added updateDevice (an existing device still being updated while the store is at the limit) is never exercised by any test — every other call uses deviceLimit 0, so updateDevice is never invoked. A regression that made updateDevice always affect 0 rows, use a wrong WHERE/SET, or unconditionally return ErrDeviceLimitReached whenever limit>0 would leave this and all other tests green. Add a case that, after the store is at the limit, calls CreateOrUpdateDevice again with the SAME DeviceID and asserts require.NoError (and ideally that client_ip/user_agent/updated_at were changed), so the update path is actually verified.

TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit only checks that a new device is rejected at the limit. It would still pass if updateDevice always returned ErrDeviceLimitReached, because it never re-submits the existing device (DeviceID "32mdo31deeqwes") at the limit. Add a call that updates the existing device with a new UserAgent or UpdatedAt, require NoError, and check the stored row changed.

issues.descricao: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before CreateOrUpdateDevice; when the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached the entry stays, so the next request from the same device skips the limit check and authenticates for up to 29 minutes.
issues.textoGolden: The `tagDeviceUI` function populates the local cache with the device ID before the `CreateOrUpdateDevice` call. If `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned, the cache entry remains set, allowing subsequent requests to bypass the device limit until the cache expires after 29 minutes.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TagDevice failures that triggered the new ErrDeviceLimitReached early-return are not permanent, because tagDeviceUI (impl.go:87) writes the device key into localCache BEFORE CreateOrUpdateDevice (impl.go:93) and never evicts it on error; tagDeviceUI returns early on any cache hit (impl.go:83-84). WHY: the first request from a new over-limit device is denied, but the poisoned cache makes every subsequent request from that same device skip the limit check entirely and authenticate successfully, so the configurable device limit is bypassed by simply retrying. HOW: only set the cache key after CreateOrUpdateDevice returns nil (e.g. move a.localCache.SetDefault after the successful DB write, or delete the key when it returns ErrDeviceLimitReached).

TagDevice now propagates ErrDeviceLimitReached to deny an over-limit anonymous device, but tagDeviceUI (impl.go:83-95) records the device in localCache at line 87 *before* calling a.anonStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the store rejects the device with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key is already cached, so the next request for that same device returns early at line 83 with a nil error and the device is admitted. The limit therefore only blocks the first request and is silently bypassed on retry. Fix by only setting the cache entry after CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds (move SetDefault after the store call), or by removing/not caching the key on failure.

The new authentication gate accepts retries from devices that were rejected by the limit because tagDeviceUI inserts the cache entry before CreateOrUpdateDevice succeeds. At capacity, the first request with a new X-Grafana-Device-Id fails, but subsequent requests with that same ID hit the 29-minute cache and receive an anonymous identity without admission to the device store. Cache only successful admissions, and ensure concurrent requests cannot treat an in-progress admission as successful.

issues.descricao: Device tagging now runs synchronously in Authenticate, adding DB round-trips on cache-miss anonymous requests where it used to be fire-and-forget.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Anonymous.Authenticate changed from fire-and-forget goroutine TagDevice to synchronous TagDevice(ctx) that runs CountDevices + INSERT/UPDATE inline. WHY: Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now blocks on two DB round-trips in the login hot path, adding latency and DB load per request where previously auth returned immediately. HOW: Restore async tagging for the non-limit path or at least decouple denial from the hot path (e.g., async count with cached count, or only synchronously enforce when near limit).

issues.descricao: The new auth.anonymous device_limit setting has no entry in conf/defaults.ini, so the GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT environment override is ignored and the limit stays 0.

comentarios.texto: The new device_limit setting is read without adding a corresponding key to conf/defaults.ini. applyEnvVariableOverrides only visits keys already present in the loaded INI and runs before readAuthSettings, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone is ignored and leaves the limit at zero, disabling enforcement. Add an uncommented device_limit = 0 entry under auth.anonymous in defaults.ini so the standard environment override mechanism can apply it.

issues.descricao: Claims ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter breaks wire dependency injection because wire.go still registers it.

comentarios.texto: ProvideAnonDBStore now takes an extra `deviceLimit int64` parameter, but pkg/server/wire.go:374-375 still lists it as a wire provider with a Bind to AnonStore. wire cannot supply an int64, so wire generation and the build fail. Remove the provider and Bind from wire.go, since impl.go now constructs the store directly.

ProvideAnonDBStore now needs a bare int64 deviceLimit, but pkg/server/wire.go (lines 374-375) still registers it as a wire provider and binds AnonStore to it. Wire has no provider for int64, so dependency injection breaks. Remove those two wire.go entries, since ProvideAnonymousDeviceService now builds the store itself, or keep the provider signature wire-compatible, for example by taking *setting.Cfg.

issues.descricao: Claims updateDevice reports ErrDeviceLimitReached for any zero-row update, conflating missing or stale devices with the limit being reached.
issues.textoGolden: The updateDevice function returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when rowsAffected == 0, but zero affected rows means the device doesn't exist or falls outside the time window, not that a limit was reached.

comentarios.texto: `ErrDeviceLimitReached` ("device limit reached") is returned for any UPDATE that affects zero rows, not only when the device limit is the cause. With MySQL the driver reports changed rows, so an UPDATE that matches an existing device but writes identical values (same client_ip, user_agent and updated_at, e.g. repeated requests within the same second) yields rowsAffected == 0 and surfaces a misleading "device limit reached" error to the authn client and logs. The identifier/message should either be renamed to reflect "device not updated/found" or the zero-row case should be distinguished from the actual limit condition.

updateDevice() reports ErrDeviceLimitReached purely from `rowsAffected == 0`. Because its WHERE clause also constrains `updated_at BETWEEN now-30d AND now+1m`, a device that simply falls outside that window (stale device, or a device id that has no matching row for any reason other than the limit) also yields 0 rows and is surfaced as 'device limit reached'. That sentinel is treated as fatal by Authenticate (client.go:45) and fails the login, so the new error is over-broad: it conflates 'device not updated' with 'limit reached' and refuses authentication for reasons unrelated to the limit. The caller distinguishes on this error, so the false positive directly causes a spurious auth failure.

issues.descricao: Claims anonymous clients can bypass the device limit by omitting the X-Grafana-Device-Id header.

comentarios.texto: The device-limit authentication gate treats requests without X-Grafana-Device-Id as admitted because TagDevice returns nil immediately for an empty header. A client can omit this client-controlled header and obtain an anonymous identity even when the configured device limit is full. When a positive limit is configured, require a valid device identifier or supply an enforced server-side identification mechanism before granting anonymous access.

issues.descricao: Claims anonymous authentication now fails entirely when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, instead of the previous non-blocking async tagging.
issues.textoGolden: Anonymous authentication now fails entirely if anonDeviceService.TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached. Previously, device tagging was asynchronous and non-blocking. This change prevents anonymous users from authenticating when the device limit is reached.

comentarios.texto: Authenticate() changed contract: device tagging used to run in a fire-and-forget goroutine with its own timeout, and any failure was only logged, so anonymous authentication always succeeded. It is now a synchronous call on the request path that returns `nil, err` for ErrDeviceLimitReached. Once the configured anonymous device limit is reached, every new/unknown device now fails anonymous authentication entirely (the broker receives an error instead of an Identity), rather than the request proceeding untagged. This consumes a request-context-dependent DB count+write synchronously on every anonymous request and turns a previously non-fatal, best-effort side effect into a hard login refusal — a caller-visible loss of availability that the surrounding auth flow was not updated to tolerate (no fallback identity is produced).

TagDevice is now called synchronously in Authenticate with the request ctx instead of in a goroutine with its own timeout. Every anonymous request that misses the local cache now waits on the DB writes and, when a limit is set, the COUNT query. If the client cancels the request, tagging is cancelled with it. Keep the async path for non-limit cases, or cache the count result.

Device tagging used to be a best-effort goroutine with its own background context and a 2-minute timeout. It now runs synchronously on the request ctx inside Authenticate, so DB latency (a COUNT query plus an upsert on every uncached request) blocks every anonymous request. The request ctx cancelling also aborts the tagging. ErrDeviceLimitReached now makes Authenticate return an error, so anonymous access is refused once the limit is hit. Decide this deliberately: either keep the tagging async where the limit is not enforced, or map the limit error to a clear client-facing response instead of a generic auth failure.

issues.descricao: Claims TagDevice now propagates all tagging errors instead of only the limit error, breaking callers that ignored them.

comentarios.texto: tagDeviceUI errors are now all returned, not only ErrDeviceLimitReached. TagDevice is called from places that previously ignored these failures, so any DB error from tagging now propagates to callers. Return the error only when it is ErrDeviceLimitReached, and keep logging other errors as before.

issues.descricao: Claims updateDevice's time window is based on device.UpdatedAt rather than time.Now(), which may not match the intended logic.
issues.textoGolden: Time window calculation inconsistency: Using device.UpdatedAt.UTC().Add(-anonymousDeviceExpiration) as the lower bound but device.UpdatedAt as the current time may not match the intended logic. Consider using time.Now().UTC() consistently.

issues.descricao: GetWebAssets does not re-check the cache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent callers that missed the cache each reload the assets manifest.
issues.textoGolden: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The exclusive lock acquired at line 48 is held (via defer on line 49) across the blocking file read / synchronous CDN HTTP request (lines 56-67) and there is no re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the lock. WHY: On a cold cache, all concurrent callers (api/index.go:82, api/frontendsettings.go:62, middleware/recovery.go:141) block on the write lock and then each sequentially re-executes the full load (file I/O or blocking http.DefaultClient.Do), producing a thundering-herd serialization and N redundant loads instead of one; in Dev mode this happens on every request since the fast path is skipped, serializing all concurrent page loads. HOW: after `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` re-check the cache (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`) so only the first goroutine performs the load, and drop the defer in favor of releasing the lock immediately after assigning `entryPointAssetsCache = result` to avoid holding it during I/O.
cache is not re-checked under the lock after re-acquiring write Lock, so concurrent callers can each recompute web assets

The cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent production requests that initially observe a nil cache each reload and decode the manifest even after another request has populated it. During a cold-start request burst, these redundant filesystem reads and JSON decodes execute serially under the global lock, delaying queued page and frontend-settings requests and blocking cache readers while each reload runs. After acquiring the write lock, return the populated cache when cfg.Env != setting.Dev before performing asset loading.

issues.descricao: Claims the cache is assigned unconditionally, so a failed load overwrites a valid cached value with nil.
issues.textoGolden: In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

comentarios.texto: The cache is assigned unconditionally, so when readWebAssetsFromFile fails, a nil result overwrites a previously valid cached value, and every caller then gets (nil, err). Only assign entryPointAssetsCache when err == nil and result != nil. On error, return the error and leave the existing cache untouched.

issues.descricao: Claims holding the exclusive lock across file and CDN I/O serializes all GetWebAssets callers.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Exclusive entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() is held across blocking file read (readWebAssetsFromFile) and HTTP fetch (readWebAssetsFromCDN). WHY: Serializes all concurrent GetWebAssets callers on disk/network latency and blocks RLock fast-path readers behind the pending writer; in Dev mode where the cache is bypassed every request serializes on file I/O. HOW: Load outside the exclusive lock (double-check, load, then lock only to publish) or use singleflight/sync.Once for the cold-miss path.

sugestoes.texto: The exported Prometheus help text says this histogram measures request sizes "returned", but QueryData observes len(v.JSON) from the incoming queries and CallResource observes len(req.Body). No response size is measured. This misleads operators interpreting the metric as returned payload volume; describe it as incoming plugin request sizes instead.

Both size-instrumented cases send empty payloads, and checkHistogram only verifies a nonzero sample count, not the observed size. Consequently, replacing the size calculations in QueryData and CallResource with a constant zero leaves this test green even though request-size instrumentation is broken. Supply nonempty query JSON and resource bodies and assert the size histogram's sample sum equals their expected byte lengths.

Both observation paths convert to float64 only after integer duration division. A 900µs plugin request is therefore recorded as 0ms, and a 1.9ms request as 1ms. This materially distorts the explicitly configured sub-millisecond histogram buckets and undercounts latency relative to the seconds metric. Divide floating-point durations in both paths instead.

issues.descricao: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh TestLogger instead of the receiver, so logs written via the contextual logger are lost to assertions on the original fake.
issues.textoGolden: The `TestLogger.FromContext` method returns a new `TestLogger` instance via `NewTestLogger()` instead of returning the receiver (f). This causes logs to be recorded on an un-referenced instance, leading to broken test assertions that expect logs to be recorded on the original logger.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh NewTestLogger instead of the receiver. WHY: LoggerMiddleware calls m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info so the write goes to a throwaway instance and assertions on the original TestLogger Calls/Message never observe it, diverging from real wrapper that preserves logger context. HOW: Return f (or a child sharing f) instead of NewTestLogger.

issues.descricao: The test function is still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware after the middleware was renamed to MetricsMiddleware.

comentarios.texto: TestInstrumentationMiddleware still carries the old name even though this PR renamed the middleware under test to MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware/NewMetricsMiddleware) and the file to metrics_middleware_test.go. The identifier advertises the superseded "InstrumentationMiddleware" name; rename it (e.g. TestMetricsMiddleware) so the test name matches the code it exercises.
Test function still named TestInstrumentationMiddleware but it constructs and asserts MetricsMiddleware (newMetricsMiddleware). Rename to TestMetricsMiddleware to match the renamed middleware.

issues.descricao: Claims ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil requests because it reads req.PluginContext without a nil guard.
issues.textoGolden: The ContextualLoggerMiddleware methods (QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) panic when a nil request is received. This occurs because they directly access req.PluginContext (via the instrumentContext function) without first checking if req is nil. This is a regression, as previous middleware layers gracefully handled nil requests.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics dereference req (req.PluginContext) without nil guard. WHY: Sibling LoggerMiddleware in same PR added explicit if req==nil guards, and direct middleware invocation with nil panics; inconsistent contract. HOW: Add same if req==nil passthrough guard before instrumentContext.

QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics dereference req (req.Queries, req.Body, req.PluginContext) without the `if req == nil` guard that LoggerMiddleware uses. A nil request panics. Add nil guards forwarding to next like LoggerMiddleware does.

QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics read req.PluginContext without checking req == nil. A nil request panics before LoggerMiddleware's guard. Add `if req == nil { return m.next.<Method>(ctx, req, ...) }` guards.

issues.descricao: Claims the refactor dropped traceID from the 'Plugin Request Completed' log lines.
issues.textoGolden: The traceID is no longer logged for plugin requests. During a refactoring, the tracing import and the logic to extract and add traceID from the context to log parameters were removed from the LoggerMiddleware. The newly introduced ContextualLoggerMiddleware does not add this information, resulting in missing traceID in plugin request logs and impacting debugging and request tracing capabilities.

comentarios.texto: LoggerMiddleware (logger_middleware.go:58) now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx) and relies on the context for all per-request attributes, but the middleware that replaced its enrichment (instrumentContext) re-adds only endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname. The traceID that logger_middleware.go previously appended itself (via tracing.TraceIDFromContext) is never put into the contextual logger, so the 'Plugin Request Completed'/grafana-data-egress line loses its traceID and log-trace correlation silently breaks. Add the trace id to the contextual attributes here (e.g. append 'traceID', tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) when non-empty) so the consumer's assumption holds.

The migration to the contextual logger dropped the traceID field. Before this PR, logRequest explicitly appended "traceID" (from tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)) to logParams. The change moved pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID into the context (ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext) and logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx), but instrumentContext does NOT add traceID. Result: "Plugin Request Completed" egress log lines silently lose their traceID, breaking correlation between plugin request logs and traces. Fix by having instrumentContext (or the logParams here) also carry the trace ID, e.g. append "traceID", tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) in instrumentContext in contextual_logger_middleware.go, or re-add it to logParams here.

The traceID key was dropped from logParams (along with the pkg/infra/tracing import) and is now expected to come from m.logger.FromContext(ctx). The only thing that populates that context is the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware.instrumentContext, which adds endpoint/pluginId/dsName/dsUID/uname but never traceID. The metrics middleware in this same PR still has to read the trace ID explicitly (metrics_middleware.go:127), confirming it is not supplied by the logger itself. Restore an explicit "traceID", tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false) entry in logParams, or have instrumentContext add the trace ID, otherwise 'Plugin Request Completed' logs lose trace correlation.

issues.descricao: Claims the metrics middleware factory mutates a shared instance's next field, causing a data race between chains.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware captures a single shared *MetricsMiddleware (`imw`) and mutates `imw.next = next` inside the middleware factory, which is re-invoked on every request because Decorator rebuilds the chain per call. WHY: concurrent requests write/read `imw.next` without synchronization, causing a data race (flagged by -race) and the possibility that a request dispatches into another request's inner chain. HOW: build a fresh instance per chain, e.g. `return plugins.ClientMiddlewareFunc(func(next plugins.Client) plugins.Client { return &MetricsMiddleware{pluginMetrics: imw.pluginMetrics, pluginRegistry: imw.pluginRegistry, next: next} })`.

WHAT: NewMetricsMiddleware reuses a single shared MetricsMiddleware instance and mutates imw.next on every CreateClientMiddleware call. WHY: Concurrent or multiple Decorator chains overwrite next on the same object causing data race and requests routed to the wrong next client, unlike Contextual/Logger middlewares that allocate per chain. HOW: Allocate a new MetricsMiddleware per chain (copy metrics handles, set next) instead of mutating the shared imw.

issues.descricao: Claims the request-size histogram's HELP text says 'returned' though it measures request sizes.

comentarios.texto: The HELP text for grafana_plugin_request_size_bytes says "histogram of plugin request sizes returned", but the metric only measures the request sent to the plugin: QueryData sums len(v.JSON) over the outgoing queries (lines 145-148) and CallResource passes len(req.Body) (line 161). Nothing "returned" by the plugin is observed. This HELP string is surfaced to users in Prometheus/Grafana metric descriptions, so it documents the opposite of the recorded value; it should describe the plugin request (egress) size, not a response size.

The metric help text describes sizes "returned", but the observations measure incoming payloads: QueryData sums len(v.JSON) and CallResource uses len(req.Body), both before invoking the plugin. This description exposes request sizes as though they were response sizes to operators reading Prometheus metadata. Change the help text to describe incoming plugin request payload sizes.

issues.descricao: Claims the test never asserts that request size is not instrumented for CheckHealth/CollectMetrics.

comentarios.texto: The request-size assertion is entirely gated behind `if tc.shouldInstrumentRequestSize`, so the `shouldInstrumentRequestSize: false` cases (CheckHealth at line 45, CollectMetrics at line 68) verify nothing about request-size instrumentation. The case names claim request size must NOT be instrumented for those endpoints, yet the body makes no assertion for them. If a regression made CheckHealth/CollectMetrics call instrumentPluginRequestSize, CollectAndCount(metricRequestSize) would become 1 and this test would still pass. Add a negative assertion for the false cases, e.g. `require.Equal(t, 0, testutil.CollectAndCount(promRegistry, metricRequestSize))`.

The shouldInstrumentRequestSize=false cases (CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) never assert that the request size metric is absent. If size instrumentation were wrongly added to those endpoints, the test would still pass. Add an else branch that requires testutil.CollectAndCount(promRegistry, metricRequestSize) to equal 0.

Missing negative assertion: when shouldInstrumentRequestSize is false (CheckHealth, CollectMetrics) the test asserts nothing about grafana_plugin_request_size_bytes. If instrumentPluginRequestSize were incorrectly called for those endpoints, CollectAndCount would be 1 yet the test would still pass. Add else branch asserting CollectAndCount==0 / histogram absent.

issues.descricao: Claims checkHistogram carries foundLabels across metrics and returns errors prematurely.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: in checkHistogram, `foundLabels` is declared before the `for _, m := range metricFamily.Metric` loop and is never reset between metrics. WHY: the counter accumulates across metrics, so the `foundLabels != len(expLabels)` check is evaluated against a stale/inflated count — a metric with only a partial label match can be accepted (false pass) and a valid metric after a partial match can error (false fail), letting the metric assertions miss real regressions. HOW: move `foundLabels := 0` inside the outer loop (reset per metric).

`foundLabels` is declared outside the `for _, m := range metricFamily.Metric` loop and never reset per metric, and the code returns an error as soon as a metric has a matching label key with a different value (rather than `continue`-ing). The correct-metric decision therefore relies on state carried over between metrics and on a premature error return instead of an exact per-metric label comparison. With more than one series in a family this produces false failures and wrong "expected N labels, got M" counts. Reset the counter per metric and `continue` to the next metric when the label set does not fully match, instead of returning an error.

issues.descricao: Claims millisecond durations are truncated by integer division before conversion to float.

comentarios.texto: The millisecond observations truncate the duration before converting it to float64: elapsed/time.Millisecond is integer division. For example, a 900µs request is recorded as 0ms and a 1.9ms request as 1ms, misclassifying observations against the fractional millisecond buckets declared above and understating the histogram sum. Use float64(elapsed)/float64(time.Millisecond) in both the exemplar and ordinary observation paths to preserve the actual duration.

Incorrect measurement: float64(elapsed/time.Millisecond) and float64(elapsed / time.Millisecond) do integer division before conversion, truncating all sub-millisecond durations to 0. Buckets start at 0.005ms so precision matters. Use float64(elapsed)/float64(time.Millisecond).

issues.descricao: Claims the request-size test cases use empty payloads and would not detect a broken size calculation.

comentarios.texto: The request-size cases pass an empty Body and no Queries, and subsequently check only that a histogram sample exists. Replacing either size calculation with a constant zero still passes this test. Use nonempty resource bodies and query JSON payloads and assert the histogram sample sum equals their expected byte count, so broken request-size instrumentation is detected.

issues.descricao: Claims the duration metric checks only labels and sample counts, not the observed values.

comentarios.texto: Both duration metrics are checked only for labels and a nonzero sample count. Observing a constant zero, or feeding seconds into the milliseconds metric, still passes. Assert the observed durations using a controlled elapsed interval (or check the relationship between the two histogram sums with allowance for millisecond truncation) so the test detects broken duration values and units.

issues.descricao: Claims the duration-seconds histogram check omits status and source labels.

comentarios.texto: Assertion too loose for duration-seconds: plugin_request_duration_seconds has labels source,plugin_id,endpoint,status,target but checkHistogram is called with only plugin_id,endpoint,target. A broken status or source label (e.g. wrong status mapping) would still pass. Require all 5 labels including status==statusOK and source==grafana-backend, and verify observed size values not just sample count.

issues.descricao: Claims LoggerMiddleware depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware running first and would log without plugin identity if reordered.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: logRequest dropped explicit pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID params and now relies solely on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) populated by upstream ContextualLoggerMiddleware.
