issues.descricao: The zh_CN totpStep1 translation is written in Traditional Chinese instead of Simplified Chinese.
issues.textoGolden: The totpStep1 value uses Traditional Chinese terms in the Simplified Chinese file (zh_CN), which is likely incorrect for this locale. Please verify the locale‑appropriate translation.

comentarios.texto: The zh_CN (Simplified Chinese) file was given Traditional Chinese characters: totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：. Compare the unchanged neighbouring lines (e.g. '打开应用扫描二维码…') which use Simplified forms; 手機/應用程式/安裝 are Traditional. zh_CN must be Simplified Chinese, so this string is in the wrong script/variant for the locale.
totpStep1 in messages_zh_CN uses Traditional Chinese (手機, 安裝, 應用程式), not Simplified Chinese as the rest of the file does. Replace it with the Simplified form: 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：
The Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 was replaced with Traditional Chinese ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一："). Use the Simplified form, "在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：".

issues.descricao: The method santizeAnchors is misspelled; it should be sanitizeAnchors.
issues.textoGolden: The method name 'santizeAnchors' should be 'sanitizeAnchors' (missing 'i').

issues.descricao: HTML_TAGS is a non-static, non-private field instead of a private static final constant.
issues.textoGolden: Field HTML_TAGS should be declared as 'private static final' following Java naming conventions for constants

issues.descricao: The diff-trimming code computes common prefix and suffix independently, so they can overlap and substring throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, crashing the verifier instead of reporting the illegal HTML.

comentarios.texto: The common prefix (start) and common suffix (end) are computed independently and can overlap, for example value "aa" vs sanitized "a". Then substring(start, length - end) gets begin > end and throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, so the verifier crashes instead of reporting the illegal HTML. Bound the suffix scan so that start + end <= min(value.length(), sanitized.length()), e.g. `while (end < min - start && ...)`.

The common prefix and common suffix are computed independently and can overlap, so `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` can have start > end and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This crashes the verifier instead of reporting 'Illegal HTML'. Cap the suffix scan with `end < Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start`.

WHAT: Common prefix/suffix stripping for the diff message can compute start+end larger than the string length and call substring(start, length-end) with start > end. WHY: Throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException inside the key loop and crashes verification instead of reporting Illegal HTML. HOW: Clamp end so start+end <= min lengths, e.g. stop suffix scan when end >= length-start.

issues.descricao: normalizeValue blanks the entire choice expression for some keys before HTML validation, so markup placed inside a choice branch of those keys bypasses the new verifier.

comentarios.texto: Choice normalization removes all branch content before HTML validation, allowing prohibited markup to bypass the new translation policy. A translated error-invalid-multivalued-size value such as `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1

WHAT: normalizeValue replaces the entire {n,choice,...} block with ... before sanitizing, so HTML inside choice options is never checked. WHY: A translation can smuggle tags (e.g. {2,choice,0#<script>...}) in error-invalid-multivalued-size/linkExpirationFormatter keys and pass the verifier, reaching UI rendering as XSS. HOW: Sanitize/validate the choice body instead of blanking it, or run the HTML policy on the inner choice text as well.

issues.descricao: The account and admin UI bundles now use Java MessageFormat placeholders and choice syntax for error-invalid-multivalued-size, but i18next expects {{n}}, so the UI shows literal {0}/{1}/{2} and the raw choice text.

comentarios.texto: The admin-ui bundle is consumed by react-i18next, which interpolates with double-brace `{{0}}` syntax (the previous value was `Attribute {{0}} ... {{2}}`). This line was rewritten to Java MessageFormat/ICU syntax (`{0}` ... `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}`), which i18next does not understand: the placeholders will not be substituted and the literal `{2,choice,...}` text will be shown to users. Keep the JS-side value in `{{0}}` form (and don't introduce ICU ChoiceFormat into the JS bundle); the ICU/choice spelling belongs only in the Java theme properties.

Same contract break in the account-ui bundle: the value was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` (i18next double-brace interpolation) and was changed to `{0}`/`{2,choice,...}` MessageFormat+ICU syntax. The account console's i18next based consumer was not updated to match, so interpolation will fail and the raw placeholder/choice syntax will be rendered. Restore `{{0}}`-style placeholders for the JS bundle.

The account-ui bundle is consumed by i18next, which interpolates with double braces (the original string was `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`). This PR aligned the value to the Java theme convention, replacing `{{0}}/{{1}}/{{2}}` with `{0}/{1}/{2}` and adding ICU `{2,choice,...}`. i18next will no longer substitute the placeholders and cannot interpret the ICU choice, so the account UI shows the raw `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2}` and literal choice text. Keep the JS-side double-brace form for this bundle (adapt the choice accordingly) rather than the Java single-brace/ICU form used by the theme messages.

issues.descricao: Claims santizeAnchors consumes English matcher groups without validation, so a translation with more anchor tags than the English text gets incorrect results.
issues.textoGolden: The anchor sanitization logic has a potential issue where it consumes English matcher groups without proper validation. If the translated text has more anchor tags than the English text, this could lead to incorrect validation results.

issues.descricao: Notes that normalizeValue blanks the whole choice expression, so a wrong argument index inside the choice would not be flagged.

comentarios.texto: normalizeValue blanks the whole choice expression, so a wrong argument index inside the choice would not be flagged. The reviewer notes this is deliberate scoping for the HTML check rather than the feature under review, and is consistent with the diff's manual sk fix.

issues.descricao: Claims the English-file path rewrite is fragile and that a messages file without an English counterpart aborts the build with a RuntimeException.

comentarios.texto: verifySafeHtml() derives the English sibling file via file.getAbsolutePath().replaceAll("resources-community","resources").replaceAll("_[a-zA-Z-_]*\\.properties","_en.properties") and opens it unconditionally, throwing a raw RuntimeException (not MojoExecutionException) on failure. The second regex is broad ('-'..'_' also matches '/', digits, and other chars), so a path with an underscore before the final path segment can be rewritten to a non-existent _en.properties, and any locale lacking an English counterpart aborts the build with an opaque RuntimeException. Restrict the substitution to the final segment and handle the missing English file gracefully.

The English reference file path is derived by regex replacement on the absolute path, and a missing file throws RuntimeException. A file with no '_' in its name, or a theme whose English file lives elsewhere, aborts the whole verification with a crash instead of adding a message to the result list. Fix: resolve the English file explicitly, and if it does not exist, treat the English value as empty or throw a proper MojoExecutionException.

The English counterpart file is opened unconditionally. If the derived path does not exist, a RuntimeException is thrown and the whole verification aborts instead of treating the English bundle as empty or reporting a message. Check that the file exists and handle its absence.

issues.descricao: Notes no test covers allowed tags under POLICY_SOME_HTML, so emptying the allow-list would not fail the suite.

comentarios.texto:
verifyIllegalHtmlTagDetected is the only test that selects POLICY_SOME_HTML (the English-has-HTML branch, line 91), but its fixture's tag is
, which is rejected by every policy. Because of this, the test (and the whole suite) still passes if POLICY_SOME_HTML's allow-list (br/p/strong/b, lines 58-61) is emptied or narrowed - i.e. if the very behaviour of permitting the allowed HTML subset in translations is broken. Add a case where the English source contains HTML and the translation uses an allowed tag (e.g. ... or
), asserting that verify() returns no 'Illegal HTML' message.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: canView(client) accepts the all-clients view permission before evaluating a client-specific permission or deny. WHY: a delegated administrator granted global view can still read a client explicitly excluded by a negative client-specific policy; ClientsResource also uses canView() to bypass all per-client checks when listing representations. HOW: reserve the global view shortcut for built-in administrative roles and evaluate the client-specific resource before falling back to the all-clients resource, including in the listing path.

WHAT: the global canView() check excludes the all-clients manage permission even though manage grants read access through canConfigure(client). WHY: an administrator with only the global manage permission can create clients but receives Forbidden from inherited requireList() and requireListClientScopes() unless separately assigned query/view roles, and cannot list client scopes despite being allowed to manage them. HOW: include the all-clients manage scope in the global read/list eligibility checks while preserving client-specific deny evaluation.

A caller granted MANAGE on all Clients passes canManageClientScopes() and canView(ClientScopeModel), but fails canView() unless separately granted VIEW. The inherited canViewClientScopes() and canListClientScopes() delegate to canView(), so this administrator can manage client scopes but cannot list them (without an additional query role). Include the global manage grant in the global view check to keep these authorization paths consistent.

The first call in this try block is getDefaultClientScopes(), which is itself forbidden before any permission is granted. Its ForbiddenException satisfies the catch, so removeDefaultClientScope() is never reached. This test would still pass if removal incorrectly allowed callers with no permissions (including a regression that denies configure-only callers but permits unprivileged callers). Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client before this block, then invoke only the removal operation inside the forbidden assertion.

The new Javadocs say these methods return true, but both methods return void. Their implementations throw ForbiddenException when the corresponding predicate is false. Document the exception contract instead, as the neighbouring require methods do, so callers are not told that denial is represented by a return value.

issues.descricao: Claims the removal-cleanup listener is guarded by the V1 fine-grained flag, so client/role/group permissions are orphaned when V1 is disabled or only V2 is enabled.
issues.textoGolden: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup is now entirely wrapped in Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), so when the feature is disabled the pre-existing removal cleanup (roles/clients/groups .setPermissionsEnabled(..., false)) no longer runs. Realms using the non-V2 permission model will keep orphaned authorization resources/permissions after a client, role or group is removed. The gate should preserve the old behavior when the feature is off (run for V1), or the V1 cleanup must be performed elsewhere.

issues.descricao: getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 only finds the type-level 'Clients' resource and returns its name, never actual client ids, so callers that resolve the returned values as client ids get wrong results or null clients.
issues.textoGolden: In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

issues.descricao: Claims getResourceTypeResource can return null in ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, causing a NullPointerException in findByResource.
issues.textoGolden: In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2 has an unused private getEvaluationContext method.
issues.textoGolden: Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

comentarios.texto: Dead computation: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and has no caller anywhere in the class. Its only possible consumer in the V1 class, `canExchangeTo`, was overridden to throw UnsupportedOperationException (line 148-150). The EvaluationContext and its overridden getBaseAttributes are built and then never used — remove the method (or wire it into canExchangeTo if token-exchange is meant to be supported).

issues.descricao: The Javadoc of the void requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() methods says they return true instead of documenting that they throw ForbiddenException.

comentarios.texto: The Javadoc for `void requireView()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}", but requireView() is void and throws ForbiddenException rather than returning a value. It is a copy-paste of the canView() doc and should read "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canView()} returns {@code false}", matching the sibling require* methods (requireListClientScopes, requireConfigure, etc.).

The Javadoc for `void requireViewClientScopes()` says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}", but the method is void and throws ForbiddenException. The doc describes a boolean return the method never produces; it should state that it throws ForbiddenException if canViewClientScopes() returns false, consistent with the other require* methods.

Declaration does not match the method it documents: the javadoc for `requireView()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}.') and for `requireViewClientScopes()` ('Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}.') describes a boolean-returning accessor, but both methods are declared `void` and are the require* counterparts that throw ForbiddenException (as documented for requireManage/requireConfigure above). The text was copy-pasted from the corresponding can* methods; it should state that the method throws when canView()/canViewClientScopes() is false.

issues.descricao: ClientPermissionsV2.canView() ignores a global MANAGE permission, so admins with only global manage take the unpaginated, per-client evaluated listing path.

comentarios.texto: canView() does not recognize an all-clients MANAGE permission even though canView(client) grants viewing through canConfigure(client) and canManage(client). For an administrator with global MANAGE but no VIEW, ClientsResource.getClients selects an unpaginated realm-wide client stream and evaluates authorization for clients before applying pagination, instead of fetching the requested database page. Include the global MANAGE permission in the global viewing capability while preserving client-specific denial semantics.

issues.descricao: canView(client) short-circuits on the global all-clients VIEW permission, so a client-specific permission denying an admin is never evaluated and the client is still viewable.

comentarios.texto: The global VIEW check returns true before evaluating client-specific VIEW permissions, bypassing a negative permission on an individual client. An administrator granted VIEW on all clients can therefore read a client explicitly excluded by a client-specific denial; ClientsResource.getClients also bypasses per-client checks when this evaluator's parameterless canView() returns true. Evaluate the specific client resource before falling back to the all-clients permission, and ensure listing does not use a global grant to skip specific denials.

Do not short-circuit resource-specific view evaluation on the global fine-grained VIEW grant. With an all-clients VIEW permission allowing an administrator and a client-specific VIEW permission denying that administrator, canView() returns true here and the specific client permission is never evaluated. This differs from the specific-over-global override behavior exercised for users in this PR and exposes the denied client's representation. Keep the administrative-role bypass separate from fine-grained grants and evaluate the client's resource before falling back to the all-clients resource; also ensure the global view result used by client listing cannot bypass those overrides.

issues.descricao: The negative check for removing a default client scope expects ForbiddenException, but it can come from the preceding getDefaultClientScopes() call, so the test passes even without a permission check on removal.

comentarios.texto: The expected ForbiddenException can come from getDefaultClientScopes(), before removeDefaultClientScope() is invoked. With no permission granted, the initial read is forbidden, so this test still passes if removal's manage-permission check is removed entirely; the later granted removal also succeeds in that broken implementation. Obtain the scope ID using the privileged realm client outside this try block, then invoke only removeDefaultClientScope() through the restricted client and assert that it is forbidden.

issues.descricao: Claims the per-client resource lookup uses server.getId() as owner while resources are created with server.getClientId(), so client-specific permissions are never found.
issues.textoGolden: In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

issues.descricao: Claims that with both fine-grained features enabled, client deletion calls ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled and throws UnsupportedOperationException.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled()/isPermissionsEnabled()/resource()/getPermissions() throw UnsupportedOperationException, but the provider listener registered in AdminPermissions.java:89-91 still calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client,false) on ClientRemovedEvent. WHY: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is not dependent on ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (see Profile.java line 58), so when both FGAP features are enabled the guard at AdminPermissions.java:77 passes, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, clients() returns the throwing V2 evaluator, and every client deletion raises UnsupportedOperationException instead of cleaning up the client's permissions. HOW: either have the listener skip setPermissionsEnabled when the evaluator is the V2 implementation, or implement setPermissionsEnabled/isPermissionsEnabled in ClientPermissionsV2 to delete/ignore the per-client resource instead of throwing.

Under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ the listener now runs and the ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). management(...) returns MgmtPermissionsV2, which this PR changed to return ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Previously clients() returned the V1 ClientPermissions and this cleanup succeeded, so deleting a client with the feature enabled now fails with UnsupportedOperationException. Guard the call (e.g. only invoke it for non-V2 / feature-disabled evaluators) or give ClientPermissionsV2 a no-op setPermissionsEnabled so the removal event no longer throws.

With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ enabled, the ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). But MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2, whose setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2"). Deleting a client therefore raises an unhandled exception inside the provider event listener (which carries its own KeycloakSession and runs inside the removal flow), breaking client removal. The listener must not invoke the V2 throwing stub — e.g. skip this cleanup for V2 or guard on the evaluator actually supporting it.

issues.descricao: Claims the all-clients resource lookup in hasPermission(String) cannot find the resource (owner mismatch or not lazily created), so global client permissions are ignored.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: hasPermission(String scope) resolves the all-clients resource with resourceStore.findByName(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, server.getId()), passing server.getId() as the ownerId, while the resource is created with owner server.getClientId() (AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource line 104) and the default findByName(ResourceServer,String) overload uses server.getClientId(). WHY: if ResourceServer.getId() differs from ResourceServer.getClientId(), the lookup never matches, this method always returns null->false, and the global 'all clients' MANAGE/VIEW/CONFIGURE permissions are silently ignored; the same 3-arg owner mismatch also appears in hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope) at line 214 (client.getId() with owner server.getId()). HOW: use the 2-arg findByName(server, name) (or pass server.getClientId() as ownerId) consistently with how the resource is created.

hasPermission(String scope) looks up the all-clients resource with findByName and returns false when it is null. That call is not guaranteed to find the resource, because it is created lazily through getResourceTypeResource, which the sibling hasPermission(client, scope) uses. As a result, canView(), canManage() and canManageClientScopes() can wrongly deny access when the all-clients resource has not been created yet. Fix: obtain the resource through AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE), as the per-client variant does.

issues.descricao: Claims the client management-permissions endpoint returns a 500 under V2 because it calls ClientPermissionsV2 methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException.

comentarios.texto: In V2, isPermissionsEnabled, resource and getPermissions now throw UnsupportedOperationException. ClientResource (around lines 710-720) calls these on permissions.clients() with no V2 guard, so the management-permissions endpoint would return a 500 instead of a clean response when V2 is active. Return a safe value (for example isPermissionsEnabled returning false) or guard the callers.

issues.descricao: Claims hasPermission(client, scope) accepts permissions granted on other resources because it does not filter by resource id, allowing privilege escalation across clients.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: hasPermission(ClientModel,String) accepts any returned Permission whose scopes contain the expected scope without checking permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId()), unlike UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission which filters by resource id. WHY: An evaluation result granting the scope on a different resource (other client or the all-clients resource when evaluating a per-client resource, or vice-versa) incorrectly authorizes the requested client — privilege escalation across clients. HOW: Filter results by resource id before matching scopes, as UserPermissionsV2 does.

issues.descricao: Claims getClientsWithPermission runs a separate policy evaluation for every client resource, causing O(N) slowdowns.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getClientsWithPermission iterates every Clients resource via findByType and calls hasGrantedPermission->evaluatePermission separately for each resource. WHY: Listing/filtering clients triggers O(N) full policy evaluations where N is the number of client authorization resources, causing material slowdown and DB/policy-store fanout on realms with many clients. HOW: Batch-evaluate once or query granted resources via a single evaluation / indexed permission lookup instead of per-resource evaluation.

sugestoes.texto: PasswordForm now treats passkey-only users as configured even when the selected theme does not render passkey authentication on the password page. With the `keycloak` theme (which inherits `base`), `createLoginPassword()` renders `base/login/login-password.ftl`, which has neither a passkeys import nor a `conditionalUIData` call, leaving these users on a password-only page despite having no password. Add the passkeys import and macro invocation to the base password template as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

issues.descricao: PasswordForm now accepts passkey-only users, but only the keycloak.v2 login-password.ftl renders the passkeys conditional UI; the base template (used by the legacy keycloak theme) does not, so a passkey-only user is shown a password-only form they cannot complete.

comentarios.texto: PasswordForm.configuredFor now accepts passkey-only users even when the active login theme renders the unchanged base login-password.ftl, which contains no passkeys UI. The legacy keycloak theme inherits that template, so a user without a password reaches a password-only challenge with no way to authenticate instead of being able to use the newly accepted passkey credential. Add the passkeys import and conditionalUIData invocation to the base login-password.ftl as well as the keycloak.v2 override.

issues.descricao: The comment 'setup webauthn data when passkeys enabled' does not mention that the condition also requires a selected user to own a passkey credential.

comentarios.texto: The new comment says webauthn data is set up "when passkeys enabled", but the guard `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` also requires that a known/already-selected user actually has a passkey credential. With realm passkeys enabled and a selected user without a passkey, `fillContextForm` is skipped (the test `passwordLogin_reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` relies on exactly this), so the comment misdescribes the condition it documents. Rephrase it to match the code, e.g. "setup webauthn data when conditional passkeys can be used (user unknown or user has a passkey)".

issues.descricao: The test comment says it sets the passwordless policy for discoverable keys, but the updater only disables passkeys for the realm.

comentarios.texto: The comment 'set passwordless policy for discoverable keys' is stale. The updater now only calls setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE), so it disables passkeys for the realm. Change the comment to say that passkeys are disabled for the realm.

issues.descricao: Claims PasswordForm.authenticate can fill passkey context data for a null user because isConditionalPasskeysEnabled returns true when no user is set, producing an inconsistent password page.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: PasswordForm.authenticate() reuses UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() whose null-user branch returns true when realm passkeys are enabled, but PasswordForm.requiresUser() is true and expects a resolved user. WHY: On a null/unresolved user (misconfigured flow, alternative execution ordering) it calls webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) without a user scope, producing a challenge/authenticators state inconsistent with the password template that now includes passkeys.ftl, causing wrong output or failed render instead of skipping passkeys. HOW: In PasswordForm use a user-required check (return false when getUser()==null or delegate only when user isConfiguredFor passkeys) rather than the null-tolerant username-form helper.

issues.descricao: Claims configuredFor marks PasswordForm as configured for passkey-only users, so they land on a password form they cannot satisfy.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: `configuredFor` now returns true via the new clause `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(user)` even when the user has no password credential at all (only a passkey). WHY: this marks the password execution as configured/required for a passkey-only user, so the flow will execute PasswordForm and render a password page for a user who has no password; if the passkey fails or the browser does not support the conditional UI/passkey, the user is left on a form whose password step can never be satisfied (badPasswordHandler on an empty/absent password), potentially stranding re-authentication/authentication. HOW: keep the passkey clause only for selecting whether to render the passkey UI, and ensure the execution still short-circuits to success when the user is already authenticated via the passwordless credential (the existing `alreadyAuthenticatedUsingPasswordlessCredential` branch), or gate the clause so it does not make PasswordForm a required step for users lacking a password credential.

issues.descricao: Claims action() processes a passkey assertion for a different userHandle during re-authentication, letting another user's passkey satisfy re-auth of the fixed user.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: New isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() per-user gate is applied to display (authenticate/challenge) but UsernamePasswordForm.action() still delegates to webauthnAuth.action() on global isPasskeysEnabled() plus presence of webauthn params without checking the fixed re-auth user owns a passkey. WHY: During re-authentication (context.getUser() fixed) an attacker/other user can POST a discoverable passkey assertion with a different userHandle and have it processed as re-auth for the fixed user, enabling user-substitution/bypass of the re-auth binding if the WebAuthn layer identifies the user from the assertion. HOW: Gate the webauthn branch in action() with isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()) or explicitly verify the asserted user equals context.getUser() when USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is set.

issues.descricao: Claims the password page leaks the typed user's passkey credential IDs to an unauthenticated visitor, disclosing whether the account has passkeys.

comentarios.texto: The password page now renders the selected user's passkey credential IDs (`authn_use_chk` hidden inputs) before the user has authenticated, since the user is only identified by a typed username. This tells an unauthenticated visitor whether the account has passkeys and discloses the credential IDs. Render the list only when the user is already authenticated, as in the re-authentication case. Otherwise leave it out and rely on discoverable credentials.

issues.descricao: Claims a Kotlin state manager should use ViewModel + StateFlow for UI state.

comentarios.texto: 所属文件夹的状态管理没有采用统一的状态管理，建议使用 ViewModel + StateFlow 管理 UI 状态。

issues.descricao: Claims UsernameForm.authenticate calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() without the required UserModel argument.
issues.textoGolden: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

issues.descricao: Claims isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, so the initial login page no longer sets up conditional passkey UI for ID-less login.
issues.textoGolden: With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

issues.descricao: Reports that widening USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH and the reauth form helper expose no sensitive data.

comentarios.texto: The change only widens visibility of the USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH constant (a boolean auth-note flag name) and replaces an inlined re-auth form setup with a call to AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context). No password, token, or user identifier is written to a log or returned; the flag is a plain "true"/"false" auth note. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

issues.descricao: Reports that setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError only toggles UI flags and leaks nothing.

comentarios.texto: AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError reads the auth note (parseBoolean) and, when set, sets the USERNAME_HIDDEN and REGISTRATION_DISABLED form attributes. It only toggles UI rendering flags; it does not emit the note value or any credential into the response or logs. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

issues.descricao: Reports that the passkey conditional-UI data is non-secret; no exposure.

comentarios.texto: The extracted isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() helper and the moved fillContextForm() calls only populate passkey conditional-UI data for the form. This is standard WebAuthn data (public credential options), not secrets, and is unchanged in kind from the pre-existing isPasskeysEnabled()/fillContextForm path. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

issues.descricao: Reports that the added error-path calls leak no credential information.

The error path continues to use the fixed "Invalid password." message (as asserted in tests) and does not leak which factor failed or any credential. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

issues.descricao: Reports that emitting WebAuthn credential IDs in passkeys.ftl is not sensitive.

comentarios.texto: The new hidden authn_use_chk inputs emit ${authenticator.credentialId}. This was specifically considered for sensitive data exposure and concluded not to be an issue: the WebAuthn credential ID is a non-secret, public identifier that is already transmitted to the server as part of every WebAuthn assertion, is only emitted for the currently-selected user's own authenticators, and follows the existing pattern used by other WebAuthn login templates. It is not a private key, password, or session secret. No sensitive data exposure issue found. No line numbers were mentioned.

issues.descricao: States the authn_use_chk field name could not be checked against the JavaScript; no problem asserted.

comentarios.texto: Unverifiable only: the authn_use_chk field name versus the JavaScript that must read it could not be checked; no mismatch is asserted.

sugestoes.texto: The invalidation check evaluates the original provider through the organization-aware getById wrapper rather than its stored enabled flag. If a public enabled provider is cached, its organization is disabled, and an administrator sets hideOnLogin=true, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because hideOnLogin is true; invalidation is skipped, so re-enabling the organization displays the now-hidden provider from the stale login query. Fetch the original model directly from idpDelegate for login-membership comparison so it uses the same stored-state semantics as the JPA login query.

The cleanup registered for each created provider removes the literal alias "alias" instead of that provider's alias, and the same mistake is repeated for idp-alias-20. TestCleanup ignores the resulting removal failures, leaving realm-level providers behind and contaminating subsequent tests or repeated executions with duplicate aliases and incorrect provider counts. Register cleanup using addIdentityProviderAlias(idpRep.getAlias()) at both creation sites.

The loop creates providers named `idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-19`, but every cleanup action removes the literal alias `alias`. Consequently these actions leave the created providers behind (and can instead remove an unrelated provider or fail on a nonexistent alias). The same mismatch occurs for `idp-alias-20` at line 425. Capture the actual created alias in each cleanup registration.

All getForLogin calls discard the returned stream and assert only internal cache contents. The implementation populates the cache eagerly, before resolving IDs and returning the providers, so replacing its final return with Stream.empty() would still pass this entire test. Consume the returned streams and assert the expected provider IDs or aliases, including a second call for an already-cached search, so the test verifies that cached login lookups actually return the correct providers.

Expanding an existing query carries forward its old organization results but assigns them a fresh revision. For example, request A reads query Q containing organization X; request B changes a provider's login eligibility in X and invalidates Q; A then invalidates the key, loads organization Y, and constructs a new query using Q's stale X results. Publishing with the current counter can accept that new query despite B's completed invalidation. Subsequent logins for X then use stale membership indefinitely (including omitting newly enabled providers). Do not carry forward an old query unless its original revision is still valid; alternatively load only the requested search result into a fresh query and use a revision/counter captured before the read.

issues.descricao: The test registers cleanup for the literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP aliases, so the created identity providers are never cleaned up.
issues.textoGolden: Cleanup reference uses incorrect alias - should be 'idp-alias-' + i instead of 'alias'.

comentarios.texto: The cleanup registers `identityProviders().get("alias")::remove` inside the loop, and also for idp-alias-20. "alias" is a literal string rather than the actual IDP alias, so none of the created IDPs is ever cleaned up. Use the real alias (e.g. the loop's alias variable / "idp-alias-20") when registering the cleanup. As written, the 21 leaked providers can skew later tests that count IDPs or login caches.

The cleanup is registered for the literal alias "alias" rather than the IDP just created ("idp-alias-" + i). The 20 created IDPs are never removed, and the same applies to the cleanup at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". Use the actual alias, e.g. get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove, so the IDPs don't leak into other tests.

The cleanup registered here uses the literal alias "alias", but the provider just created has alias "idp-alias-" + i. The same mismatch is repeated at line 425 for "idp-alias-20". The cleanup can never find/remove the created providers (null dereference/404 on remove, or at best a silent no-op), so none of the 21 IDPs this test creates are cleaned up and the realm is left polluted for later tests. Use the actual alias, e.g. `testRealm().identityProviders().get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove` and `get("idp-alias-20")::remove`.

issues.descricao: On a partial cache miss getForLogin merges the previously read login query into a newly revisioned entry, so a concurrent invalidation can be lost and stale IDP IDs for other organizations persist.

comentarios.texto: Do not merge the previously read query into a newly revisioned entry without verifying its revision. A reader can obtain a query containing organization A's IDs, then another transaction disables a provider or changes its organization and invalidates this key. When the reader requests an uncached organization B, this branch obtains a fresh revision but copies the old A results into the new query and publishes it using the current counter. Subsequent A requests receive stale membership indefinitely (a disabled or moved provider still exists, so the null-ID fallback does not repair it). Rebuild rather than copy after invalidation, or ensure the old query's revision is still valid atomically before publishing the merged entry.

issues.descricao: Login-cache invalidation on update compares the organization-aware enabled state, so changing a broker to private while its organization is disabled skips invalidation and leaves the now-private IDP in the cached login list.

comentarios.texto: The early return compares the original IDP's organization-aware enabled state rather than the persisted enabled state used to populate the login cache. If a cached public IDP's organization is disabled and an admin changes BROKER_PUBLIC to false, the original predicate is false because the organization is disabled and the updated predicate is false because the broker is private, so the stale ID remains cached; re-enabling the organization displays the now-private broker because the login bean only rechecks isEnabled. Compare raw persisted models for login-cache invalidation, for example by loading the original through idpDelegate.getById before applying this predicate.

issues.descricao: The LoginFilter javadoc still claims its constants are all criteria for login availability although getLoginPredicate now also checks organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now also filters on organization link plus the BROKER_PUBLIC config (line 254), but the enum's javadoc directly above (lines 215-217) still states that the enum "contains all fields that are considered when deciding if a provider should be available for login or not", presenting ENABLED/LINK_ONLY/HIDE_ON_LOGIN as the exhaustive criteria. Any reader — or a future LoginFilter constant added against that documented assumption — will believe organization link and BROKER_PUBLIC play no role. Update the javadoc to include the organization-link/public-broker condition, or move the condition into a documented LoginFilter constant.

issues.descricao: The login-cache test creates only public org-linked IDPs, so the new BROKER_PUBLIC check in getLoginPredicate is not covered.

comentarios.texto: Test fixture never covers the new BROKER_PUBLIC branch: all org-linked IDPs are created public, so reverting the getLoginPredicate public-check leaves all counts unchanged and the test still passes. Add at least one org-linked non-public (BROKER_PUBLIC false/missing) enabled IDP and assert it is excluded from getForLogin counts.

issues.descricao: The test never consumes or asserts getForLogin's returned providers and never repeats a query, so the cache-hit path that builds the result is untested and could return wrong IDPs without failing.

comentarios.texto: Consume and assert the results of getForLogin, including a repeat query for the same mode/organization to exercise a cache hit. All calls in this test discard the returned stream and assert only IdentityProviderListQuery contents. The implementation populates that query before reconstructing the returned models, so returning an empty stream (or the wrong providers) at line 254 would still pass the entire test. Assert the expected provider identities on both the initial query and the cached query, rather than only the internal cached count.

issues.descricao: Claims getForLogin re-enters the caching layer by calling session.identityProviders().getById instead of idpDelegate.getById; this deliberately resolves IDs through the per-IDP cache.
issues.textoGolden: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.

issues.descricao: Claims the cache-hit path of getForLogin returns raw, non-organization-aware models; getById already wraps them.

comentarios.texto: Cache-hit path in getForLogin returns raw getById results without createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel applied on miss/fallback paths, changing the return-shape contract by cache state. Wrap hit-path results the same way before returning.

The new getForLogin override wraps results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel on every non-cached path (lines 218 and 249) but the cache-hit loop adds the raw model returned by session.identityProviders().getById(id) directly. Any consumer that relies on the organization-aware model (as documented by the 're-check isEnabled as idp might have been wrapped' comment added in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) therefore receives a different model shape whenever the list happens to be served from cache. Add .map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel) (or wrap before adding to the set) in this loop so the returned shape is identical on cache hit and cache miss.

issues.descricao: Claims linking/unlinking an IDP to an organization never invalidates the getForLogin caches; the org provider routes through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update which does.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: The new getForLogin cache (keyed by realm+FetchMode via cacheKeyForLogin) is only invalidated from this provider's create/remove/update methods, but linking/unlinking an IDP to/from an organization is performed by InfinispanOrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider (model/infinispan/.../organization/InfinispanOrganizationProvider.java:249-270), which only calls registerOrganizationInvalidation(organization) and never registers cacheKeyForLogin invalidation. WHY: After an org-link mutation that does not itself route through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update(), the ORG_ONLY and ALL login caches keep returning the pre-mutation ID set, so the login page shows an IDP linked to (or no longer linked to) an organization until some unrelated update/create/remove happens to invalidate the key. HOW: Register cacheKeyForLogin invalidation for all FetchMode values from the organization provider's addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider (or ensure those paths delegate through the IDP storage provider's update so registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate runs).

WHAT: Login cache invalidations only fire from IdP create/update/remove, with no invalidation when an IdP is linked/unlinked to an organization via OrganizationProvider.addIdentityProvider/removeIdentityProvider. WHY: getForLogin results depend on organizationId/BROKER_PUBLIC, so linking/unlinking leaves the cached ID sets in IdentityProviderListQuery stale and login pages show/hide the wrong brokers until eviction.

issues.descricao: Claims resolving cached IDs one by one with getById turns login listing into N lookups; those lookups hit the per-IDP cache by design.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: Cached getForLogin() resolves every cached internalId with an individual session.identityProviders().getById(id) call in a loop. WHY: Turns one login-broker listing (hot login path) into N per-ID lookups, O(N) growth with broker count with per-miss DB fallback and invalidation retry.

issues.descricao: Claims the HashSet in cached getForLogin returns IDPs in nondeterministic order; every caller sorts the result.

comentarios.texto: getForLogin accumulates the login IDPs into `new HashSet<>()` and returns `identityProviders.stream()`. A HashSet provides no iteration-order guarantee, so the cached path returns the IDPs in arbitrary/hash order, unlike the delegate path and the non-cached branch which preserve the delegate's ordering. Any caller of getForLogin that does not re-sort now receives non-deterministic ordering for cached results (and it can differ between cache-hit and cache-miss). Preserve the delegate order (e.g. use a LinkedHashSet and iterate the cached ids in their stored order, or sort the result) so the cached and non-cached paths are consistent.

issues.descricao: Claims remove() of a nonexistent alias now dereferences null; the new login invalidation is null-safe and the other call is unchanged pre-existing code.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: remove() stores idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) in storedIdp and calls registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) when the alias key is invalid without a null check. WHY: Removing a non-existent alias causes null dereference on idp.getInternalId() instead of a clean false return.

issues.descricao: Claims getLoginPredicate can NPE on a null config; config is always initialized.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: getLoginPredicate() dereferences idp.getConfig().get(...) without null-checking getConfig(). WHY: A model with null config throws NPE inside the predicate used by create/remove/update invalidation and cached filtering, crashing the invalidation path.

issues.descricao: Claims org-specific ALL/ORG_ONLY login queries include non-public org IDPs, so the BROKER_PUBLIC gate misses invalidations; the query always requires BROKER_PUBLIC=true.

comentarios.texto: getLoginPredicate now declares an org-linked IDP to be a login IDP only when BROKER_PUBLIC is true (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC))`). This predicate is the sole gate for login-cache invalidation: create/remove call registerIDPLoginInvalidation(idp) and update calls registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated), both of which skip invalidating the `.idp.login.<FetchMode>` caches whenever the predicate says the IDP is not a login IDP. However, FetchMode.ALL/ORG_ONLY for a specific organization are the org's own login view and include the organization's linked IDPs regardless of BROKER_PUBLIC (BROKER_PUBLIC only controls the realm-level page). A non-public, org-linked IDP is therefore treated as non-login and its creation/removal/enable-disable/move-into-org does not invalidate the login caches, so those caches keep serving the stale set of IDPs for the org. The predicate's org/BROKER_PUBLIC condition needs to be scoped to the fetch modes it actually applies to (realm-level membership), or the invalidation must be driven by the full set of IDs each mode can return.

The login-cache invalidation is gated exclusively by getLoginPredicate(), which (newly, server-spi IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254) treats an org-linked IDP as a login IDP only when BROKER_PUBLIC is true. But the cache this method guards, produced by getForLogin() (same file, lines 214-255), stores for ORG_ONLY/ALL the ids of the org's own IDPs (as used with a concrete organizationId in OrganizationCacheTest line 406), which can include org-linked non-public broker IDPs. For such an IDP, both original and updated fail the predicate, so registerIDPLoginInvalidation() and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate() skip invalidation (the latter via its early `!test(original) && !test(updated)` return), leaving the ORG_ONLY/ALL cache entries stale when the IDP's public/hideOnLogin flag is toggled or its org link is directly reassigned; getForLogin()'s null-id self-heal only catches deletions, not these membership changes. The invalidation must cover every IDP the login caches can contain, not only those matching the public-org predicate.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The new table visualization receives hard-coded empty rows, metadata, and columns instead of the query result. WHY: Every dashboard table using the use-table-widget-visualization feature renders empty even when its query returns data. HOW: Pass result.data and result.meta to tableData and derive columns from the configured fields, or retain the existing table until the result adapter is implemented.

WHAT: The attribute query cache key omits organization identity although its query function calls an organization-specific endpoint. WHY: Switching organizations with matching project filters (especially all-projects selection), date range, dataset, and attribute type reuses the previous organization's cached attribute names in the destination organization's search UI until refetch completes. HOW: Include organization.slug in the query key and its memo dependencies so cache entries remain tenant-scoped.

WHAT: Both custom-cell fallback checks test truthiness instead of whether the callback returned undefined. WHY: Valid custom results such as 0 or null are replaced by default content, causing incorrect numeric output or preventing callers from intentionally hiding cell content. HOW: Use cell !== undefined in both the head and body renderer checks to preserve the documented fallback contract.

The new story documents that returning undefined invokes the fallback renderer, and the callback explicitly returns React.ReactNode | undefined. However, this truthiness check also invokes fallback for valid custom results such as 0, an empty string, or null (commonly used to suppress cell content). A caller following that contract can therefore display the original field value instead of its intended custom content. Check specifically for undefined here and in the equivalent header callback.

The Visualize instances now expose only yAxis, but static/app/views/explore/savedQueries/exploreParams.tsx:29 still computes `visualizes.flatMap(visualize => visualize.yAxes)`. That consumer must be migrated along with the class: it now collects undefined rather than the visualization expressions, breaking the saved-query visualization display (and failing type checking if these are typed as Visualize). Update that consumer to map `visualize.yAxis`; serialized BaseVisualize consumers should continue using yAxes.

The new query key omits the organization identity, unlike the previous key whose URL included organization.slug. For the same filters (in particular all-project selections), switching organizations reuses the previous organization's TagCollection. Attribute names can contain customer-specific or sensitive identifiers and can now appear in another organization's autocomplete; depending on cache freshness, a refetch does not prevent the cached data from being shown. Include the organization slug or ID in the query key.

The new React Query key contains only query options, none of which identifies the organization. Two organizations with identical project/date selections (especially the all-projects selection) therefore share an entry despite fetching different organization-scoped URLs. Switching organizations can serve the previous organization's attributes, and concurrent consumers can reuse its in-flight request. Include organization.slug in this cache key.

These validators test truthiness instead of presence. Both age=0 and timestamp=0 are accepted integer values, so a report containing both fields with those values passes validation, violating the explicitly declared requirement that they cannot coexist. Check membership in initial_data instead of the values' truthiness (and cover the zero-valued case in the mixed-fields test).

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this caller discards the fetched result and passes empty columns, rows and metadata. The new TableWidgetVisualization consumes these props directly (`columns ?? ...` and `data={tableData?.data ?? []}`), so it cannot infer or fetch the missing result: every dashboard table becomes empty for enabled organizations even when the query returns rows. Pass the result data and metadata, and either derive the requested columns or omit columns to use the component's metadata fallback.

The mutual-exclusion checks test values rather than field presence. Both fields accept 0, so a report containing both `age: 0` and `timestamp: 0` passes validation even though the fields must be mutually exclusive. Check membership in initial_data in both validators instead.

The renderer contract uses `undefined` to request fallback, but `if (cell)` also discards valid ReactNode values including `0`, an empty string, false, and null. For example, a custom renderer returning 0 for a computed count instead renders the original data through the default renderer. Use an explicit undefined check here and in the equivalent header-renderer check.

When use-table-widget-visualization is enabled, every table receives empty columns and empty data instead of the result being mapped here. Consequently populated dashboard tables appear empty. Pass the actual result data/meta and corresponding columns to the visualization.

The query function requests an organization-specific URL, but queryKey contains only filter options. Switching organizations with identical project/date/type options (particularly all-project selection) reuses the previous organization's attribute collection, potentially displaying its keys until a refetch completes. Include the organization slug in the query key as the old URL-based key did.

These validators promise to reject simultaneous age and timestamp fields, but test their values rather than their presence. A report containing both age=0 and timestamp=0 is accepted, even though timestamp=0 is explicitly valid and age=0 is a normal fresh report. Check key presence to enforce the stated exclusivity for zero values too.

issues.descricao: The age/timestamp mutual-exclusion validators check truthiness via initial_data.get(), so a zero value is treated as absent and a report carrying both fields passes validation.
issues.textoGolden: Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

comentarios.texto: The timestamp/age validators test truthiness and make both fields optional instead of enforcing exactly one field. Reports with both age=0 and timestamp=0, or with neither field, pass validation despite violating the stated mutually exclusive report formats. Enforce field presence and exclusivity in object-level validate using key membership rather than truthiness.

Check key presence rather than truthiness when enforcing age/timestamp mutual exclusion. Both fields permit 0, so a report with age=0 and timestamp=0 passes both validators even though both fields are present; a zero-valued counterpart also bypasses the corresponding check. Use `"age" in self.initial_data` and `"timestamp" in self.initial_data` (or object-level validation) and add zero-value tests.

Check field presence rather than truthiness when enforcing timestamp/age exclusivity. A report containing both `timestamp: 0` and `age: 0` passes both validators, despite the declared constraint that they must not coexist; with only one zero value, validation is also asymmetric. Use membership checks on initial_data (or object-level validation) and add zero-value mixed-field tests.

issues.descricao: The validation-failure warning logs the entire raw, attacker-controlled browser report instead of a redacted subset.

comentarios.texto: The new validation-failure warning logs `raw_report`, the full unvalidated report object supplied by the caller. This endpoint is public and unauthenticated (permission_classes = (), @csrf_exempt), so the payload is attacker-controlled, and browser report bodies routinely carry sensitive values (CSP blocked-uri/document-uri/script-sample, sourceFile, plus the full user_agent). Logging the raw payload on every validation failure writes potentially sensitive data into application logs; log only the report `type` (or a sanitized/redacted subset) instead of the entire raw object.

Do not attach the complete raw report to the validation warning. Browser reports contain page URLs (potentially including tokens or personal data in query strings) and arbitrary body contents. Any invalid field now causes that entire payload to be emitted at warning level, exposing it in operational logs even where the existing info-level request logging is filtered out. Log the failed field names/report type or a redacted diagnostic instead.

issues.descricao: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids positionally with nodestore get_multi values, but get_multi does not preserve input order (cached items are appended last) and drops missing nodes, so error details get attached to the wrong error IDs.
issues.textoGolden: Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).

comentarios.texto: WHAT: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with events.values() instead of mapping by node_id, misaligning ids to payloads and dropping/mismatching on missing keys. WHY: assigns wrong title/message/timestamp to wrong error id and yields incorrect Seer logs. HOW: look up each node_id in the get_multi dict (e.g. dict keyed by node_id) and preserve error_ids order.

`zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` values preserve input order and that all keys exist. Dict values give no such guarantee; missing keys shorten/misalign the zip, attaching the wrong event payload to the wrong error_id. Lookup per-id: iterate node_ids/error_ids and do `events.get(node_id)` instead of zipping with `.values()`.

fetch_error_details pairs IDs to payloads with zip(error_ids, events.values()) where events is dict from nodestore get_multi. Values order need not match IDs and missing keys misalign, attaching wrong title/message to wrong error. Look up per node_id instead.

issues.descricao: The Snuba replay lookup for error IDs runs even when enable_error_context=false, adding a needless query (and failure point) to opt-out requests.

comentarios.texto: The new Snuba replay lookup executes even when enable_error_context=false. Every opt-out summary request incurs an unnecessary database round trip and can now fail on Snuba availability even though it only needs recording storage. Evaluate the flag first and perform the replay lookup only when error context is enabled.

issues.descricao: With the use-table-widget-visualization flag on, the widget renders TableWidgetVisualization with hardcoded empty columns and data instead of the query results, so every table widget shows an empty table.
issues.textoGolden: Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: the `use-table-widget-visualization` branch renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, hardcoding empty rows and no columns instead of the actual query result. WHY: when the feature flag is enabled for an org, every table widget renders an empty table and silently drops `result.data`/`result.meta`/`columns`, a functional regression for all dashboard table widgets. HOW: build `columns`/`tableData` from the existing `result` (and `widget.queries[i].fields`/`fieldAliases`) rather than the empty placeholder objects.

In the new feature-flagged branch, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with hardcoded empty props: columns={[]} (an empty array, which is truthy for the `columns ?? fallback` logic, so no columns are derived) and tableData={data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}. All the real result data computed above (result.data, result.meta, fields, fieldAliases, eventView) is discarded, so any organization with 'use-table-widget-visualization' enabled gets an empty table instead of the query results. Pass the actual result data/columns into the visualization (or keep the old StyledSimpleTableChart) until the widget is properly wired.

With the 'use-table-widget-visualization' feature enabled, TableWidgetVisualization is rendered with columns=[] and empty data/meta instead of result.data and result.meta. Every table widget therefore renders empty for orgs with the flag. Fix: pass tableData={{data: result.data, meta: result.meta}} and build columns from the fields.

issues.descricao: The custom cell renderers fall back to default rendering on any falsy return (0, '', null), not only undefined, so a renderer cannot render zero or an empty cell.

comentarios.texto: The documented custom-renderer contract says fallback runs when the callback returns undefined, but `if (cell)` also falls back for valid ReactNode results such as `0`, an empty string, or `null`. A caller trying to render zero or deliberately suppress a cell instead gets the default field rendering. Check `cell !== undefined` here and in the head-cell renderer so the implementation honors the advertised contract.

Use `cell !== undefined` instead of `if (cell)` to select the custom renderer result, and apply the same correction to the header renderer. The API documents undefined as the fallback sentinel, but valid ReactNode results such as numeric 0, an empty string, or null are falsy. A custom renderer returning 0 or intentionally hiding a cell with null therefore unexpectedly renders the default value instead.

issues.descricao: The attribute-keys query key no longer includes the organization slug, so two organizations with the same filters share a cache entry and switching orgs can show the previous org's attribute names.

comentarios.texto: The new attribute query key omits the organization even though its query function fetches an organization-specific endpoint. Switching organizations with identical project selections such as all projects and the same date range reuses the singleton query client's prior organization's attribute metadata, including while the new request refetches. Include organization.slug or organization.id in the query key.

Include the organization slug in this query key. The new useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys implementation fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions contains no organization identity. Two organizations with identical filters (particularly the default all-project selection) therefore share this cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attribute names, and concurrently mounted consumers can reuse a request for the wrong organization. Preserve the organization-specific cache identity that the previous endpoint-based key provided.

Include the organization slug or ID in this query key. The query function fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`, but the key contains only query options. Two organizations with the same project selection (especially the all-projects selection), date range and dataset therefore share a cache entry. Switching organizations can display the previous organization's attributes, and overlapping requests can populate the shared entry with the wrong organization's result.

issues.descricao: The UseTraceItemAttributeBaseProps doc says only LOGS is supported, although the hooks are also used with SPANS.

comentarios.texto: The new shared prop documentation claims the endpoint currently supports only LOGS, but this PR also uses these hooks with TraceItemDataset.SPANS (for example in TransactionNameSearchBar). Update this comment to describe both supported datasets; as written it incorrectly tells callers that a supported and actively used input is unsupported.

issues.descricao: Claims the unauthenticated endpoint iterates an unbounded array of reports, allowing CPU/metric-spam DoS.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: endpoint loops over unbounded raw_data array validating each report and metrics.incr per report with no size limit. WHY: attacker can POST huge arrays causing CPU/memory blowup and metric spam on unauthenticated endpoint. HOW: enforce max reports per request (e.g. reject >50) before validation.

issues.descricao: Claims BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns Django HttpResponse objects although its Endpoint base expects DRF Response objects.
issues.textoGolden: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.

issues.descricao: The assemble analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check, so requests rejected with 404 are still counted as assemble events, skewing analytics.
issues.textoGolden: Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

comentarios.texto: The 'preprod_artifact.api.assemble' analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check at line 88 (and before any validation). When the organization lacks 'organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble' the endpoint returns 404 without assembling anything, but the assemble event has already been emitted, so this metric/analytics event over-counts requests that never performed the operation. Move the analytics.record call to after the feature check (once assembly is actually attempted/succeeds) so the event reflects the operation it names.

WHAT: analytics.record runs before the preprod-artifact-assemble feature check, logging assemble attempts even when disabled/unauthorized. WHY: inflates analytics, leaks usage signal, and does work before guard. HOW: move analytics.record after the feature check (or after validation).

issues.descricao: BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update() reads validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of 'type', so detector type changes are silently ignored.
issues.textoGolden: In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

comentarios.texto: WHAT: update() reads validated_data.get("detector_type") but the field/validate_type stores it as "type", so type updates are silently ignored. WHY: PUT type change never applies, breaking caller assumption and diverging from create() which uses validated_data["type"]. HOW: read validated_data.get("type", instance.group_type).

issues.descricao: Claims get_condition_query_groups indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] and may KeyError for a DCG missing from the precomputed map.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: get_condition_query_groups directly indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] which KeyErrors if data_condition_groups contains an id absent from the precomputed map. WHY: crashes delayed-workflow task and blocks firing/retries. HOW: use .get(dcg.id, []) or ensure map covers all dcgs.

WHAT: get_groups_to_fire directly indexes dcg_to_slow_conditions[dcg.id] with same missing-key risk as query-groups path. WHY: same task crash during evaluation when DCG sets drift. HOW: use .get with default and handle missing.

issues.descricao: Claims the triggered_actions log now writes the full event payload with user data because event_data was switched to workflow_event_data.

comentarios.texto: The log extra 'event_data' now holds workflow_event_data, which wraps the full event object, instead of the ids-only EventRedisData. This writes event payloads that can contain user data (messages, tags, user and request context) to logs. Log only identifiers instead, such as event_id, group_id and workflow ids.

issues.descricao: Claims the success path dereferences data.summary without guarding undefined data when the query is disabled or errored.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: success path dereferences data.summary/numFeedbacksUsed without guarding data undefined (disabled/error-transition states). WHY: throws cannot-read-property crash when query is disabled or returns no data. HOW: guard (data?.summary ?? null) and handle undefined data.

issues.descricao: Claims the column fallback crashes when tableData is defined but meta is missing.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: column fallback uses tableData?.meta.fields without guarding meta, so defined tableData with missing meta throws TypeError. WHY: crashes render on empty/error payloads instead of empty table. HOW: use tableData?.meta?.fields with fallback to [].

issues.descricao: Claims ExploreParams still reads visualize.yAxes after the Visualize class switched to yAxis, producing undefined saved-query params.

comentarios.texto: Replacing Visualize.yAxes with yAxis leaves consumers in savedQueries/exploreParams.tsx:29 and components/seerSearch.tsx:179 reading the removed property. Those consumers now obtain undefined instead of visualization fields, breaking the existing contract and potentially TypeScript compilation. Update those consumers to use yAxis or serialize through toJSON as appropriate.

The removal of the instance `yAxes` field was not followed through to `static/app/views/explore/savedQueries/exploreParams.tsx:29`, which still computes `visualizes.flatMap(visualize => visualize.yAxes)`. Those accesses now produce undefined rather than the selected aggregate fields, breaking construction of saved Explore parameters. Update that consumer to map `yAxis` (while retaining arrays in the serialized contract).

`static/app/views/explore/components/seerSearch.tsx:179` still constructs its visualization payload with `yAxes: v.yAxes`. With instances now exposing only `yAxis`, that payload loses its aggregate selection instead of supplying the array the Seer consumer expects. Update this consumer to use `[v.yAxis]` or the serialized `toJSON()` representation.

issues.descricao: Asks to verify that no caller passes Visualize instances instead of BaseVisualize to updateLocationWithAggregateFields.

comentarios.texto: It was not verified whether any caller passes Visualize instances (rather than BaseVisualize) to updateLocationWithAggregateFields. If one does, those instances would be stringified in a shape that the new isBaseVisualize reader rejects, so the values would be lost or ignored when read back. Check all callers of updateLocationWithAggregateFields and make sure they pass BaseVisualize objects, or convert Visualize instances via toJSON() first.

issues.descricao: Claims the number-type test's mock matches query.query instead of substringMatch, so its not-called assertion can never fail.

comentarios.texto: The number-type test's mock matches on `query.query === 'search-query'`, but the hook under test sends the search string as `substringMatch` (see traceItemAttributeValuesQueryKey in useGetTraceItemAttributeValues.tsx, and the correct predicate in the first test in this file). That mock can never be selected, so `expect(searchQueryMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` is satisfied regardless of whether the number-type short-circuit exists — the assertion no longer witnesses the behavior the test names. Fix the predicate to `query.substringMatch === 'search-query'` (and, better, assert the call did occur and returned [] to pin the guard).

The number-type test's mock matcher checks `query.query === 'search-query'`, but the hook sends the search as `substringMatch`. The mock can never match, so `expect(searchQueryMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` passes even if the number short-circuit were removed. Match on `query.substringMatch` as the string-type test does, so the not-called assertion can actually fail.

The mock for the number-type test matches `query.query === 'search-query'`, but `traceItemAttributeValuesQueryKey` sends the search as `substringMatch`. If the numeric early-return guard is removed, the hook will issue a request that does not match this mock, so `expect(searchQueryMock).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` still passes instead of detecting the forbidden request (and the test may fail only due to an unmatched-request error). Match `substringMatch`, as the string-type test does, so this test directly detects regression of the no-request behavior.

issues.descricao: Claims the attribute key is interpolated into the request path without encodeURIComponent, enabling path confusion.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: attributeKey (tag.key) is interpolated raw into /trace-items/attributes/${attributeKey}/values/ without encodeURIComponent. WHY: keys containing /, brackets or encoded chars break routing or allow path confusion/smuggling to unintended endpoints. HOW: encodeURIComponent(attributeKey).

issues.descricao: get_environment_info fetches the recommended event per issue while building the merged-PR comment, an N+1 lookup on the comment path.

comentarios.texto: WHAT: get_environment_info calls issue.get_recommended_event() per issue inside the merged-PR comment loop. WHY: N fetches (DB/Snuba/nodestore) per comment generation amplifies latency on the PR-comment path. HOW: batch/prefetch recommended events or skip environment lookup when unavailable.

sugestoes.texto: WHAT: The new isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) guard is false for workers created by multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process. WHY: A hung worker is left running when its replacement is started, so both can flush the same Redis queues if the old worker resumes, causing duplicate production and retaining untracked processes. HOW: Check against self.mp_context.Process (or multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess) before killing the worker.

WHAT: join breaks out of the worker loop when the shared deadline expires, skipping cleanup of all remaining workers. WHY: If next_step.join consumes the timeout, or one worker stalls until the deadline, subsequent workers remain alive and untracked after shutdown or rebalancing. HOW: Apply the deadline only to waiting, and still run process termination for every worker using the spawn-context process type.

WHAT: submit calls get_memory_info once for every process-specific buffer even though each call retrieves memory information for the entire Redis cluster. WHY: With P flusher processes, every submission performs P redundant cluster-wide INFO operations serially on the consumer thread, multiplying network traffic and blocking time precisely when parallel flushing is enabled. HOW: Query memory information from one buffer only; SpansBuffer.get_memory_info does not filter by assigned_shards.

The new docstring promises one process per shard, but the implementation caps the process count at max_processes and assigns multiple shards to each process when that cap is smaller than the shard count. In particular, the CLI defaults to one flusher process for all assigned shards. Document the cap and shared-shard behavior so callers do not infer per-shard parallelism or isolation that is not provided.

Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not a subclass of the default-context multiprocessing.Process class. Consequently this isinstance check is false for real workers. When a worker is declared hung, it is left running while a replacement is started and its handle is overwritten, allowing multiple workers to operate on the same shards and leaving the old worker unmanaged. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or the spawn context's Process class) instead.
